STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.claim: The final section again warns against denying God's signs and persisting in idolatry.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.anchor: repeats the warnings about denying the signs of God and persisting in idolatry

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.claim: The surah closes with devotional practices, including invoking God's Names and listening to Quran recitation.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r30.anchor:
several verses dealing with pious and
devotional practices, including invoking the Names of God and
listening to the recitation of the Quran (vv. 180, 204–5).

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p458/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p458/r13.speaker: الجهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p458/r13.claim: Jahm also argues شيء names even the lowest or nonexistent things and does not express divine perfection, unlike the beautiful names.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p458/r13.anchor: ولله الأسماء الحسنى والاسم إنما يحسن لحسن مسماه

BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r1.claim: The beautiful names are the most excellent names because they point to the finest and noblest meanings.
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r1.anchor: تأنيث الأحسن أي الأسماء التي هي أحسن الأسماء وأجلها لأنها دالة على معاني هي أحسن المعاني وأشرفها

BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r2.claim: Names are vocal expressions assigned to meanings, so a name differs from what is named; otherwise the named would equal the number of names, an impossibility.
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بها الألفاظ الدالة الموضوعة على المعاني المختلفة دل على أن الاسم غير المسمى

BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r3.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r3.claim: Al-Ghazali distinguishes the name, the act of naming, and the named as three different, non-synonymous things.
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r3.anchor: قال الإمام الغزالي : الحق أن الاسم غير التسمية وغير المسمى فإن هذه ثلاثة أسماء متباينة غير مترادفة

BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r4.claim: God is to be invoked and remembered through these names; the passage also quotes the statement that disbelievers' prayer is error (40:50).

BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r5.speaker: الحديث
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r5.claim: A hadith promises Paradise to whoever enumerates God's ninety-nine names and then supplies their list.
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r5.anchor: إنتسعة وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحدا من أحصاها دخل الجنة

BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r6.speaker: المشايخ المتقدمون
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r6.claim: Early Sufi masters recommend beginning a supplication with the divine names in vocative form and ending with blessings on Muhammad and his family and a request for provision.
BURSEVI:v3p215#2/r6.anchor: واستحسن المشايخ المتقدمون أن يبدأ أولا ويقول اللهم إني أسألك يا رحمن يا رحيم

BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r1.claim: The name Allah is greatest because it denotes the all-comprehensive essence bearing every divine attribute; other names denote individual meanings such as knowledge or power.
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r1.anchor: اسم الله أعظم الأسماء التسعة والتسعين لأنه دال على الذات الجامعة لصفات الإلهية كلها

BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r2.claim: Allah is the most specific name and cannot be applied to another literally or figuratively, while names such as capable, knowing, and merciful can be used of others.
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r2.anchor: ولأنه أخص الأسماء إذ لا يطلقه أحد على غيره لا حقيقة ولا مجازا وسائر الأسماء قد يسمى بها غيره

BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r3.claim: Scholars treat the other divine names as being referred back to Allah, as this verse demonstrates.
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r3.anchor: وقد جعل العلماء من خصائص هذا الاسم أنه ينسب جميع أسماء الحق إليه

BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r4.speaker: شيخنا
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r4.claim: The Shaykh maps four divine self-disclosures onto life and the unseen, knowledge and the realm of meanings, will and spirits, then power and the visible world.
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r4.anchor: قال حضرة شيخنا العلامة أبقاه الله بالسلامة في بعض تحريراته : واعلم أن الهوية الإلهية السارية في جميع المراتب

BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r5.speaker: شيخنا
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r5.claim: The four realms correspond to God as Living, Knowing, Willing, and Powerful and as First, Last, Manifest, and Hidden, yielding four root realities.
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r5.anchor: هو الحي العليم المريد القدير وهو الأول والآخر والظاهر والباطن وبذلك السريان ظهرت الحقائق الأربع

BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r6.speaker: شيخنا
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r6.claim: The Shaykh derives 16, 32, 33, and then 99 universal names by combining four roots with four worlds, manifestation and concealment, unity, and hearing, sight, and speech.
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r6.anchor: ثم باعتبار الظهور والبطون صارت اثنين وثلاثين ، ثم باعتبار أحدية جمع الجميع كانت ثلاثا وثلاثين

BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r7.speaker: شيخنا
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r7.claim: The Shaykh connects the count of 100 with the Prophet's practice of thirty-three tasbih, tahmid, and takbir after prayer, completed by a final tahlil.
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r7.anchor: ثلاثا وثلاثين تكبيرة ثم تمم المائة بقوله : لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له له الملك

BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r8.speaker: شيخنا
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r8.claim: The Shaykh derives 1,001 names from the five presences and their manifest and hidden aspects; seven roots underlie them, while their particulars are countless.
BURSEVI:v3p216#2/r8.anchor: ثم كانت ألفا باعتبار تعيناتها في الحضرات الخمس من جهة الظهور والبطون

BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r1.claim: People should avoid the deviants' heresy to escape its punishment; leaving those who deviate means abandoning their misnaming, since leaving the people themselves makes no sense.
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r1.anchor: واتركوا تسمية الزائغين فيها بتقدير المضاف إذ لا معنى لترك نفس الملحدين

BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r2.claim: Some scholars understand the beautiful names as God's exalted attributes, since name can mean a celebrated description or reputation.
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : المراد بالأسماء الحسنى الصفات العلى فإن لفظ الاسم قد يطلق

BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r3.claim: The Najmiyya commentary treats Allah as the proper name of the Essence and the remaining names as names of attributes; Allah is un-derived according to its view and most scholars.
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r3.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : {ولله الاسمآء الحسنى} يشير إلى أن اسم الله له بمثابة اسم العلم للخلق

BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r4.claim: Names derived from essential attributes such as life, hearing, sight, speech, knowledge, power, will, and permanence are eternal and uncreated.
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r4.anchor: صفات الذات كالحياة والسمع والبصر والكلام والعلم والقدرة والإرادة والبقاء قديمة غير مخلوقة

BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r5.claim: Names derived from acts are created and apply upon creation: God is called Creator and Provider when He creates and provides, though He eternally had that capacity.
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r5.anchor: وصفات الفعل مخلوقة تضاف إليه عند الإيجاد فلما أوجد الخلق وأعطاهم الرزق سمي خالقا ورازقا

BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r6.claim: On this interpretation, the verse's beautiful names means God's beautiful attributes.
BURSEVI:v3p217#2/r6.anchor: ولله الأسماء الحسنى ، أي : الصفات الحسنى

BURSEVI:v3p218/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p218/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p218/r1.claim: Calling on God by names derived from His attributes entails cultivating those qualities through sound actions and intentions; the creative quality is expressed through marriage for offspring.
BURSEVI:v3p218/r1.anchor: فادعوا الله بكل اسم مشتق من صفة من صفاته بأن تتصفوا وتتخلقوا بتلك الصفة

BURSEVI:v3p218/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p218/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p218/r2.claim: A person embodies God's provision-giving attribute by spending God's provision on those in need rather than hoarding it.
BURSEVI:v3p218/r2.anchor: والاتصاف بصفة الرازقية بأن ينفق ما رزقه الله على المحتاجين ولا يدخر منه شيئا

BURSEVI:v3p218/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p218/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p218/r3.claim: Spiritual embodiment comes through polishing the heart, guarding it from attachment to anything besides God, and turning toward Him for the disclosure of His attributes.
BURSEVI:v3p218/r3.anchor: وأما التخلق بها فبالأحوال وذلك بتصفية مرآة القلب ومراقبته عن التعلق بما سوى الله والتوجه إليه

BURSEVI:v3p218/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p218/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p218/r4.claim: The author identifies this spiritual state with the sacred report that God becomes the servant's hearing and sight.
BURSEVI:v3p218/r4.anchor: وهذا تحقيق قوله : "كنت له سمعا وبصرا فبي يسمع وبي يبصر"

BURSEVI:v3p218/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p218/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p218/r5.claim: Deviation in God's names means turning away from His attributes by failing to embody them.
BURSEVI:v3p218/r5.anchor: يميلون في صفاته أي لا يتصفون بها

BURSEVI:v3p218/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p218/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p218/r6.claim: Calling God names He did not give Himself is deviation; the philosophers' First Cause and Necessary-by-Essence imply that He lacks choice in creating.
BURSEVI:v3p218/r6.anchor: وتسميته تعالى باسم لم يسم به نفسه أيضا من الإلحاد كما يسمونه الفلاسفة بالعلة الأولى والموجب بالذات

BURSEVI:v3p218/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p218/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p218/r7.claim: Describing God with an attribute unsupported by revealed text is also deviation.
BURSEVI:v3p218/r7.anchor: ومن وصفه تعالى بوصف أو بصفة لم يرد بها النص فأيضا إلحاد

BURSEVI:v3p218#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p218#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p218#2/r1.claim: The Najmiyya commentary says deviants will be abandoned to act by nature and desire in the same way they practiced deviation in names and attributes.
BURSEVI:v3p218#2/r1.anchor: ما كانوا يعملون بالإلحاد في الأسماء والصفات انتهى كلام "التأويلات"

ELMALILI:7:172-181/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181/r8.claim: The rendering instructs people to invoke God by His most beautiful names and leave those who deviate regarding them to their coming recompense.
ELMALILI:7:172-181/r8.anchor: Allah’ındır en güzel isimler (esmâ-i hüsnâ) onun için siz O’na onlarla çağırın ve O’nun isimlerinde sapıklık eden mülhidleri bırakın

ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r6.claim: God is one and incomparable, not a merely numerical unity that could have a partner; He is self-sufficient and gathers all attributes of perfection.
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r6.anchor: Allah zâtında birdir, ehaddır ve ism-i zâtı bir Allah’tır. Fakat vâhid-i adedî gibi şerîk ü nazîri bulunabilecek fakir bir vahdetle değil

ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r7.claim: The multiplicity of God's names and attributes does not entail multiplicity in His essence; His names point to divine attributes of supreme perfection.
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r7.anchor: sıfât u esmânın kesreti zât ve müsemmânın ta‘addüd ve kesretini iktizâ etmeyeceğinden

ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r8.claim: The majestic plural in divine speech signals the collected grandeur of God's essence, attributes, and names while affirming His unity.
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r8.anchor: hitâbât-ı ilâhiyede vârid olan انا، شهدنا، ذرأنا gibi cem‘-i azamet, bu zât ve sıfât ve esmânın mertebe-i cem‘iyyetindeki azamet ü kibriyâyı

ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r9.claim: Believers should call upon, remember, and describe God by His most beautiful names.
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r9.anchor: o esmâ-i hüsnâ, o en güzel isimler ile dua, zikr ediniz veya O’nu bunlarla tavsif ve yâd ediniz

ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r10.claim: Elmalılı warns against names that carry a false or bad implication or fail to express utmost perfection, illustrating this with Bedouin invocations such as “Abā al-Makārim” and “Abyad al-Wajh.”
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r10.anchor: bedevîlerin ،يَا أَبَا الْمَكَارِم، يَا أَبـْيَضَ الْوَجْهِ يَا نجي demeleri gibi sû’-i îhâmdan

ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r11.claim: Ilḥād includes rejecting al-Raḥmān or objecting to God's majestic names, applying names reserved for God to others, and deriving idol names al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā from Allah and al-ʿAzīz; believers should leave such people to their recompense.
ELMALILI:7:172-181#3/r11.anchor: Allah’a mahsus olan esmâ-i hüsnâyı Allah’ın gayrısına aynen ıtlak, yahut Arap müşriklerinin putlarına “Allah” isminden te’nîs ile اَل َّلات ve “el-Azîz” isminden اَلْعُ َّزى

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r1.claim: Esmāʾ al-ḥusnā means Allah’s names that denote all His most beautiful and perfect qualities; words expressing His attributes also belong to it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r1.anchor: Allah Teâlâ’nın hepsi de en güzel ve en mükemmel olan niteliklerine, özelliklerine delâlet eden isimleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r2.claim: The Qur’an gives Allah more than one hundred names, hadiths attribute others, and the technical term is commonly taken to mean the ninety-nine names collected in a hadith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r2.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de Allah’ın 100’den fazla ismi yer almakta; ayrıca hadislerde O’na başka isimler de nisbet edilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r3.speaker: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r3.claim: He says these names express Allah’s transcendence and greatness and awaken reverence in people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r3.anchor: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabî şu görüşleri ileri sürmektedir: 1. Bu isimler, Allah hakkında yücelik ve aşkınlık ifade eder, kullarda da saygı hissi uyandırır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r4.speaker: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r4.claim: He says invoking these names in remembrance and supplication helps prayers be accepted and earns reward.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r4.anchor: 2. Zikir ve dua olarak okunduğunda kabule vesile olur, sevap kazandırır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r5.speaker: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r5.claim: He says the names bring peace to hearts and instill hope for mercy.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r5.anchor: 3. Kalplere huzur verir, rahmet ümidi aşılar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r6.speaker: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r6.claim: He says understanding and reciting the names of the highest being also elevates the reciter.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r6.anchor: 4. En yüce varlık olan Allah’ın isimlerini, anlamlarını kavrayarak okumak, okuyanın değerini de yüceltir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r7.speaker: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r7.claim: He says the names express what is necessary, possible, and impossible regarding Allah, so knowing them helps form sound belief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r7.anchor: 5. Bu isimler Allah hakkında zorunlu, mümkün ve imkânsız olan inançları ve kanaatleri ifade ettiği için bu isimleri bilip okumak doğru inancın oluşmasına da katkıda bulunur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r8.claim: Names and attributes are reminders and partial introductions to their referent, not the referent itself; human understanding cannot encompass Allah, though the words intend Him.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r9.claim: Because the Qur’an and hadith invoke Allah by these names, pronouncing them carries the worship value of remembrance, glorification, and supplication.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r9.anchor: müminin bunları telaffuz etmesi zikir, tesbih, dua gibi kelimelerle ifade edilen bir ibadet değeri taşır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r10.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r10.claim: The Prophet promises Paradise to those who memorize Allah’s ninety-nine names and internalize the beliefs their meanings teach.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r10.anchor: bir hadiste Hz. Peygamber, Allah’ın doksan dokuz isminin bulunduğunu, bunları ezberleyip benimseyen (anlamlarını öğrenip bu isimlerin telkin ettiği inancı özümseyen) kimselerin cennete gireceğini müjdelemiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r11.claim: Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah give a list of ninety-nine names after the hadith, but some listed names do not occur in the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r11.anchor: Tirmizî ve İbn Mâce’nin Sünen’lerinde (Tirmizî, “Da‘avât”, 83; İbn Mâce, “Duâ”, 10) bu açıklamadan sonra doksan dokuz ismin listesi de verilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r12.speaker: bazı âlimler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r12.claim: Some scholars argue that the lists in Tirmidhī and Ibn Mājah were a narrator’s personal additions, not part of the original hadith.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r12.anchor: bazı âlimler anılan iki kaynaktaki listenin hadisin aslından olmayıp râvinin kişisel tesbiti ve eklemesi olduğunu savunmuşlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r13.speaker: İbn Hacer el-Askalânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r13.claim: Ibn Hajar compiled a new list of ninety-nine beautiful names from names found in the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r13.anchor: İbn Hacer el-Askalânî, Kur’an-ı Kerîm’deki isimlerden yeni bir doksan dokuz esmâ-i hüsnâ listesi oluşturmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r14.claim: People should invoke Allah by His beautiful names alone, never assign them to another or treat anything else as His equal or divine.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r14.anchor: insan, bu isimlerle Allah’a yakarışta bulunmalı, yalnız Allah’a verilebilecek olan bu güzel isimleri O’ndan başkasına vermemeli

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r15.claim: Ilḥād means departing from truth and moderation; one form is using names reserved for Allah, with their divine meanings, for another.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r15.anchor: ilhâd, “haktan sapmak, itidalden ayrılmak” anlamına gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r16.claim: A second kind of deviation is describing God with names and attributes exclusive to created beings, such as father or son.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r16.anchor: Allah’ı, baba oğul gibi sadece yaratılmışlara özgü isim ve sıfatlarla anmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r17.claim: A third kind of deviation is denying God’s names outright or interpreting and distorting them in a way that amounts to denial.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r17.anchor: Allah’ın isimlerini tamamen inkâr etmek veya böyle bir sonuç doğuracak şekilde te’vil ve tahrif etmek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r18.claim: Those who distort the beautiful names from their true meanings are condemned and warned that their ill-intentioned conduct will be punished.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r18.anchor: gerçek anlamlarından saptıranlar kınanmakta, onların bu kötü niyetli tutumlarının cezasını görecekleri uyarısında bulunulmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r19.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r19.claim: The verse also warns against people who flatter rulers, leaders, heroes, or sheikhs so excessively that their words place the praised person in an almost divine position.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:180/r19.anchor: övdüğü kişiyi âdeta tanrısal bir konumda gösteren ifadeler kullanmaları konusunda da önemli ve yararlı bir uyarı değeri taşımaktadır

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p146.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p146.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p146.claim: The call to God by His beautiful names returns to the pledge of monotheism innate in human nature at 7:172, after the intervening account of people who disregarded revelation and became blind and deaf.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p146.anchor: This verse relates to verse 172 in which the pledge of monotheism found in human nature is mentioned

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.claim: Ascribing partners, sons, daughters, or other unbecoming attributes to God denies His power, knowledge, and uniqueness; only attributes befitting His oneness should be affirmed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.anchor: ascribe partners to Him or assign sons and daughters to Him negate His attributes of power, knowledge and peerlessness

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.claim: Ilḥād here means disrespecting God’s names and attributes by assigning Him derisive or unfitting descriptions from which He is exalted.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.anchor: they ascribe names and attributes to God which are not befitting for His majesty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.claim: Leaving those who distort God’s attributes means consigning their case to Him; they will soon be punished for their actions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p147.anchor: Leaving such people alone means to consign their matter to God

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r1.claim: These readers pronounce the initial yāʾ in yalḥidūn with ḍamma in al-Aʿrāf and the parallel verses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر: يلحدون بضم الياء، وكذلك في سورة النحل [103]، والسجدة [40].

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r2.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r2.claim: Hamza opens both the yāʾ and ḥāʾ in all three occurrences.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة الأحرف الثلاثة بفتح الياء والحاء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r3.speaker: الكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī opens yāʾ and ḥāʾ in al-Naḥl but uses ḍamma on the yāʾ in al-Aʿrāf and al-Sajda.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي في النحل: لسان الذي يلحدون إليه بفتح الياء والحاء

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r4.claim: The form ilḥād is supported by the related Qurʾanic word and by the more familiar noun mulḥid; lāḥid is rarely heard.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r4.anchor: حجة من قرأ: يلحدون قوله: ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد [الحج/ 25]، ويدل على أن ألحد أكثر، قولهم: ملحد

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن وغيره
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r5.claim: Alḥada and laḥada are two dialect forms, so a reader alternating them may be drawing on both.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r5.anchor: وزعم أبو الحسن وغيره: أن ألحد ولحد لغتان: فمن جمع بينهما في قراءته، فكأنه أراد الأخذ بكل واحد من اللغتين

FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r6.claim: Ilḥād means deviating from the straight course; a laḥd is a grave niche cut into the side, unlike a central shaft.
FARISI-HUJJA:v4p107#3/r6.anchor: وكأن الإلحاد: العدول عن الاستقامة والانحراف عنها، ومنه اللحد: الذي يحفر في جانب القبر خلاف الضريح

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r6.claim: يلحدون is read from ألحد or لحد; both forms mean to incline or deviate, and the word لحد also names the side niche of a grave.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p167/r6.anchor: فالحجة لمن ضم الياء وكسر الحاء أنه أخذه من ألحد يلحد والحجة لمن فتحهما أنه أخذه من لحد يلحد وهما لغتان

IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r4.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r4.claim: They read يلحدون with ḍamma on yāʾ, as also in al-Nahl and al-Sajda; Hamza opens yāʾ and ḥāʾ in all three forms.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r4.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم وأبو عمرو ﴿ يلحدون ﴾ بضم الياء وكذلك فى النحل 103 والسجدة 40

IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r5.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r5.claim: Al-Kisai opens yāʾ and ḥāʾ in the al-Nahl form, but reads the Araf and al-Sajda forms like Abu Amr.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p297/r5.anchor: وقرأ الكسائى فى النحل ﴿ الذين يلحدون ﴾ بفتح الياء والحاء وقرأ فى الأعراف ﴿ يلحدون ﴾ مثل أبى عمرو

QIRAAT-ER:7:180:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:7:180:12#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:7:180:12#1/r1.claim: Form I yalḥadūna means incline or dig laterally, while Form IV yulḥidūna means cause deviation or commit ilḥād; the first foregrounds physical action and the second causative abstraction.
QIRAAT-ER:7:180:12#1/r1.anchor: Form I foregrounds the physical action; Form IV foregrounds the causative-abstract meaning.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p244#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p244#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p244#2/r1.claim: Qatada glosses those who deviate in God’s names as deviating in His signs, meaning that they associate partners with Him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p244#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه ﴾ يقول في آياته قال يشركون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r7.speaker: ابن السكيت
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r7.claim: Laḥada and alḥada can both mean turning from truth and introducing something foreign to it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r7.anchor: هو العدول عن الحق والإدخال فيه ما ليس منه قاله ابن السكيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r8.claim: The triliteral and quadriliteral forms can mean deviation from uprightness, and the quadriliteral is more common; a poet uses الملحد, while laḥd also names the grave's sloping side.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r8.anchor: وقال غيره: العدول عن الاستقامة والرباعي أشهر في الاستعمال من الثلاثي وقال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r9.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī distinguishes alḥada as leaning away from lḥada, which means resorting to or inclining toward something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p213/r9.anchor: وقيل ألحد بمعنى مال وانحرف ولحد بمعنى ركن وانضوى قاله الكسائي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r7.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r7.claim: Maqātil reports that a man invoked Allah once and al-Raḥmān once in prayer; Abū Jahl objected that Muhammad's followers claimed one Lord, and the verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r7.anchor: قال مقاتل: دعا رجل الله تعالى في صلاته ومرة دعا الرحمن، فقال أبو جهل:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r8.claim: The verse follows the warning about people made for Hell by naming a kind of them who distort God's names, especially Abū Jahl and his peers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r8.anchor: لما ذكر أنه ذرأ كثيرا من الجن والإنس للنار ذكر نوعا منهم وهم الذين يلحدون في أسمائه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r9.claim: After linking Hell with heedlessness of God's remembrance, the text directs people to remember Him through His beautiful names and exalted attributes as a way out of punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r9.anchor: والمخلص من العذاب هو ذكر الله أمر بذكر الله بأسمائه الحسنى وصفاته العلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r10.claim: A heart absorbed in worldly desires moves from one craving and demand to another and falls into darkness; Abu Ḥayyān says he observed this experientially.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r10.anchor: والقلب إذا غفل عن ذكر الله وأقبل على الدنيا وشهواتها وقع في الحرص، وانتقل من رغبة إلى رغبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r11.claim: He gives the example of someone making up all missed prayers together; opening the heart to remembrance frees it from heedlessness and enables obedience and avoidance of prohibitions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230/r11.anchor: حتى إن أحدهم ليصلي الصلوات كلها قضاء في وقت واحد فإذا انفتح على قلبه باب ذكر الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the names are best because they indicate good meanings such as praise and sanctification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r1.anchor: التي هي أحسن الأسماء لأنها لا تدل على معان حسنة من تحميد وتقديس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r2.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine form of al-aḥsan; a singular feminine adjective can properly describe a non-rational plural, though matching the plural would use the pattern al-ḥusun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r2.anchor: فالحسنى هي تأنيث الأحسن ووصف الجمع الذي لا يعقل بما يوصف به الواحدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r3.speaker: unidentified exegete
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r3.claim: Another grammatical analysis treats al-ḥusnā as a verbal noun used adjectivally.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the names here unanimously mean the named entities or designations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r4.anchor: والأسماء هاهنا: بمعنى التسميات إجماعا من المتأولين لا يمكن غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r5.claim: Abu Ḥayyān says Ibn ʿAṭiyya's formulation is imprecise: tasmiya is a verbal noun, whereas the verse means words used of God whose descriptions differ while the described One remains the same.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r5.anchor: ولا تحرير فيما قال لأن التسمية مصدر والمراد هنا الألفاظ التي تطلق على الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r6.claim: A name used to invoke God as beautiful must be established by revelation and explicitly applied to Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r6.anchor: وكون الاسم الذي أمر تعالى أن يدعى به حسنا هو ما قرره الشرع ونص عليه في إطلاقه على الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r7.claim: Calling upon God by the names means addressing Him with names such as Allah, al-Raḥmān, and Mālik.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r7.anchor: ومعنى فادعوه بها أي نادوه بها كقولك: يا الله يا رحمن يا مالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also construes the command as naming Him by those names, like saying that one named his son ʿAbd Allāh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r8.anchor: فسموه بتلك الأسماء جعله من باب دعوت ابني عبد الله أي سميته بهذا الاسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r9.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r9.claim: Al-Bāqillānī permits applying an unreported name that conveys pure praise and has no ambiguity or shared meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r9.anchor: فنص القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني على الجواز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r10.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r10.claim: Al-Ashʿarī forbids applying such an unreported name; the jurists and majority agree, and Abu Ḥayyān endorses their position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r10.anchor: ونص أبو الحسن الأشعري على المنع، وبه قال الفقهاء والجمهور وهو الصواب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r11.claim: Some allow restricted active participles derived from Quranic actions such as mocking or plotting, while others forbid them; Abu Ḥayyān prefers forbidding even restricted forms, and unqualified forms are unanimously forbidden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r11.anchor: فجوز ذلك فرقة ومنعت منه فرقة وهو الصواب وأما إطلاق اسم الفاعل بغير قيده فالإجماع على منعه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r12.speaker: الترمذي عن أبي هريرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r12.claim: Al-Tirmidhī transmits from Abū Hurayra a report listing ninety-nine divine names one by one; Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes irregularities in some names and says the list report is not mutawātir.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p230#2/r12.anchor: وروى الترمذي في جامعه من حديث أبي هريرة النص على تسعة وتسعين اسما مسرودة اسما اسما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says some entries in the individually listed ninety-nine-name report are anomalous and that this report is not mutawātir, although al-Tirmidhī called it gharīb and its sole transmitter Ṣafwān ibn Ṣāliḥ is trustworthy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r1.anchor: وفي بعضها شذوذ وذلك الحديث ليس بالمتواتر وإن كان قد قال فيه أبو عيسى هذا حديث غريب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r2.claim: Abu Ḥayyān clarifies that calling the report mutawātir is not technical hadith usage; it is an individual-chain report.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r2.anchor: تسمية هذا الحديث متواترا ليس على اصطلاح المحدثين في المتواتر وإنما هو خبر آحاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r3.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r3.claim: The soundly transmitted saying is that God has ninety-nine names, one short of one hundred, and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise; enumeration means counting, memorizing, believing, revering, and reflecting on their meanings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r3.anchor: إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحد من أحصاها دخل الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r4.claim: A prayer of the Prophet includes Yā Ḥannān, Yā Mannān, which is not found in al-Tirmidhī's Jāmiʿ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r4.anchor: وفي بعض دعاء رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «يا حنان يا منان»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r5.claim: Among scholars who composed explanations of the beautiful names are al-Ghazālī, Ibn al-Ḥakam ibn Barrajān, al-Rāzī, and Ibn al-ʿArabī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r5.anchor: وقد صنف العلماء في شرح أسماء الله الحسنى كأبي حامد الغزالي وابن الحكم بن برجان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests that the verse refers to God's beautiful attributes, such as justice, goodness, and beneficence, and their dissimilarity from creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r6.anchor: ولله الأوصاف الحسنى وهي الوصف بالعدل والخير والإحسان وانتفاء شبه الخلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r7.claim: On this reading, deviants describe God as willing evils, creating indecency, or possessing creature-like attributes such as being seen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r7.anchor: فيصفونه بمشئية القبائح وخلق الفحشاء والمنكر وبما يدخل في التشبيه كالرؤية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says to leave deviants alone without arguing or confronting them; on this reading the verse is abrogated by fighting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r8.anchor: اتركوهم ولا تحاجوهم ولا تعرضوا لهم قاله ابن زيد فتكون الآية على هذا منسوخة بالقتال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says deviants use impermissible names for God or refuse some revealed names; examples include calling Him Abū al-Makārim or refusing al-Raḥmān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r9.anchor: يقولون: يا أبا المكارم يا أبيض الوجه يا سخي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r10.claim: Mujāhid explains deviation as naming idols al-Lāt after Allah and al-ʿUzzā after al-ʿAzīz, calling God a father, and naming idols lords.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r10.anchor: قاله مجاهد، ويسمون الله أبا وأوثانهم أربابا ونحو هذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ilḥād means lying.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: معنى يلحدون يكذبون،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r12.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r12.claim: Qatāda says ilḥād means associating partners with God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r13.speaker: الخطابي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r13.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī defines error and deviation concerning God's names as ilḥād.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r13.anchor: الغلط في أسمائه والزيغ عنها إلحاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r14.claim: Ḥamza and the named readers read yalḥadūn with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ; the other five canonical readers read yuḷḥidūn with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r14.anchor: وقرأ حمزة: يلحدون بفتح الياء والحاء وكذا في النحل والسجدة وهي قراءة ابن وثاب والأعمش وطلحة وعيسى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r15.claim: The warning encompasses deviation in God's names as well as all their other ugly acts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p231/r15.anchor: واندرج تحت قوله ما كانوا يعملون الإلحاد في أسمائه وسائر أفعالهم القبيحة

QASHANI:7:179-180/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:179-180/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:179-180/r3.claim: Each divine name is the Essence together with an attribute, and God governs each affair through one of His names.
QASHANI:7:179-180/r3.anchor: كل اسم هو الذات مع صفة، والله يدبر كل أمر باسم من أسمائه

QASHANI:7:179-180/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:179-180/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:179-180/r4.claim: Invoke God by the name suited to one's need; inward appeal means attaining readiness to receive that name's effect, such as knowledge, healing, or wealth.
QASHANI:7:179-180/r4.anchor: إذا طلب العلم يدعوه باسمه العليم، والمريض إذا طلب الشفاء يدعوه باسمه الشافي

QASHANI:7:179-180/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:179-180/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:179-180/r5.claim: Verbal invocation works through the intended name: saying Lord can mean the Knowing, Healer, or Enricher according to the need addressed.
QASHANI:7:179-180/r5.anchor: وأما بلسان القال كما إذا قال الأول: يا رب، يريد به يا عليم، لاختصاص ربوبيته بذلك الاسم

QASHANI:7:179-180/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:179-180/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:179-180/r6.claim: Invocation through action means taking on the divine attribute: surrendering one's knowledge to God's knowledge, healing others by His healing, or becoming free of need through Him.
QASHANI:7:179-180/r6.anchor: وأما بلسان الفعل كما يدعوه الطالب السالك باتصافه بتلك الصفة

QASHANI:7:179-180/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:179-180/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:179-180/r7.claim: This is the invocation commanded to monotheist believers, who should comply.
QASHANI:7:179-180/r7.anchor: وهذه هي الدعوة المأمور بها الموحدون من المؤمنين فليمتثلوا

QASHANI:7:179-180/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:179-180/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:179-180/r8.claim: Those who deviate in God's names seek His attributes from other than Him and ascribe them elsewhere, thereby associating partners.
QASHANI:7:179-180/r8.anchor: وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه } يطلبون هذه الصفات من غيره ويضيفونها إليه فيشركون به

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r1.claim: Ilhad means turning away from the right course, either by adding to the truth or subtracting from it.

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r2.claim: Anthropomorphists deviate by excess, while those who negate divine attributes deviate by deficiency.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r2.anchor: فأهل التمثيل زادوا فألحدوا ، وأهل التعطيل نقصوا فألحدوا

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r3.claim: God's customary order leaves the world with people who sustain its flourishing and keep the truth manifest.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r3.anchor: ألا يخلي البسيطة من أهل لها هم الغياث وبهم دوام الحق في الظهور

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r4.claim: God's people summon others to truth, direct them to it, act and rest through it, and stand by it as succor for creation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r4.anchor: هدايتهم بالحق أنهم يدعون إلى الحق

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r5.claim: These spiritual helpers bring relief: people receive rain in drought and their prayers are answered.

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r6.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r6.claim: One account of spiritual delusion is imagining oneself close to God when one's share in destiny is actually separation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r6.anchor: أن يلقى في أوهامهم أنهم من أهل الوصلة

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r7.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r7.claim: Another account is gaining a good reputation among people while concealing evil from God.

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r8.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r8.claim: Another account is that every increase in companionship is accompanied by a decrease in spiritual rank.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r8.anchor: ويقال الاستدراج ألا يزداد في المستقبل صحبة إلا ازداد في الاستحقاق نقصان رتبة

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r9.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r9.claim: Another account is falling from an imagined pure state into reprehensible action; a truly sincere state would protect conduct.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r9.anchor: ويقال الاستدراج الرجوع من توهم صفاء الحال إلى ركوب قبيح الأعمال

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r10.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r10.claim: Another account is making grand claims that arise from diseased meanings.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r10.anchor: ويقال الاستدراج دعاوى عريضة صدرت عن معان مريضة

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r11.speaker: ويقال
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r11.claim: Another account is receiving abundant favor without giving thanks.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r11.anchor: ويقال الاستدراج إفاضة البر مع ( . . . ) الشكر

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r12.claim: Reflection on the Messenger's character and the effects of divine nearness shows that his testimony is not fabricated.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r12.anchor: ليشهدوا أخلاق آثار التقريب بجملة أحواله - عليه السلام - ليعلموا أن ذلك الشاهد ليس بشاهد متخرص

QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r13.claim: The Prophet's nearness is fragrant, but only those with experiential gnosis can perceive its scent; others cannot report his true state.
QUSHAYRI:v1p370/r13.anchor: يدرك ذلك النشر إلا بشم العرفان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r1.claim: The verse instructs believers how to remember God and how to deal with those who neglect Him, following the account of their heedlessness; the author promises another explanation later.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r1.anchor: قيل : تنبيه للمؤمنين على كيفية ذكره تعالى وكيفية المعاملة مع المخلين بذلك الغافلين عنه سبحانه وتعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r2.speaker: حجة الإسلام العزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r2.claim: Al-Ghazali and others define names as spoken forms indicating distinct meanings; “most beautiful” means best in naming because the meanings are finest and most noble.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بالأسماء كما قال حجة الإسلام العزالي وغيره الألفاظ المصوغة الدالة على المعاني المختلفة والحسنى أنيث الأحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r3.claim: An alternative understands “names” as attributes, as in the expression that someone’s name has spread through the lands, meaning his reputation and description.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r3.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالأسماء الصفات ويكون من قولهم طار إسمه في البلاد أي صيته ونعته

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r4.claim: The majority prefers names as spoken forms because “call upon Him by them” fits naming God or addressing Him with those names.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r4.anchor: والجمهور على الأول لقوله عز إسمه : ( ( فادعوه بها ( لأنه إما من الدعوة بمعنى التسمية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r5.claim: Ilhad means turning away from truth and uprightness toward falsehood; the word derives from the side recess of a grave.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r5.anchor: أي يميلون وينحرفون فيها عن الحق إلى الباطل يقال : ألحد إذا مال عن القصد والإستقامة ومنه لحد القبر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r6.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r6.claim: Hamza reads the verb here and in Fussilat with the fatḥa form from the triliteral verb; the meaning remains the same.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ حمزة هنا وفي فصلت ( يلحدون ) بالفتح من الثلاثي والمعنى واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة عن الأحمر
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r7.claim: Al-Ahmar distinguishes alhada as disputing from lahada as deviating; al-Wahidi prefers the majority reading because the latter form is rarely heard with that meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r7.anchor: وروى أبو عبيدة عن الأحمر أن الحد بمعنى مارى وجادل ولحد بمعنى مال وانحرف واختار الواحدي قراءة الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r8.claim: Ilhad in God’s names includes calling Him by names without scriptural warrant or by names suggesting a corrupt meaning, such as Bedouin praise names; believers must avoid such usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r8.anchor: والإلحاد في أسمائه سبحانه أن يسمى بما لا توقيف فيه أو بما يوهم معنى فاسدا كما في قول أهل البدو يا أبا المكارم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r9.speaker: أبو القاسم القشيري
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r9.claim: Those interpreting ilhad this way hold that God’s names are textually specified: only names established in the Qur’an, Sunnah, or consensus may be used.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r9.anchor: ذهب إلى أن أسماء الله تعالى توقيفية يراعى فيها الكتاب والسنة والإجماع فكل إسم ورد في هذه الأصول جاز إطلاقه عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r10.claim: The author rejects the suggestion that the verse’s use of “names” means mere human designations and therefore omits a pronoun.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r10.anchor: وما قيل : إنه أريد بالأسماء التسميات فلذا ترك الإضمار ليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r11.speaker: الآمدي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r11.claim: Al-Amidi denies that rational proof or analogy licenses divine names; otherwise “jurist” or “intelligent” would be preferable labels simply because their meanings apply.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r11.anchor: ليس مأخذ جواز تسميات الأسماء الحسنى دليلا عقليا ولا قياسا لفظيا وإلا لكان تسمية الرب تعالى فقيها عاقلا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r12.speaker: الآمدي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r12.claim: For names neither expressly permitted nor forbidden, some scholars prohibit them while al-Amidi says the sound position is to suspend judgment and follow revealed evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r12.anchor: فقد قال بعض أصحابنا بالمنع منه ليس القول بالمنع مع عدم الدليل أولى من الآخر بل الحق في ذلك هو الوقف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r13.speaker: الآمدي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r13.claim: Al-Amidi says apparent scriptural evidence suffices; certainty is not required for either permission or prohibition because both are legal rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r13.anchor: وهو أن يكون ظاهرا في دلالته وفي صحته ولا يشترط فيه القطع كما ذهب إليه بعض الأصحاب

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r14.claim: The author notes the familiar distinction between foundational or creedal rulings and practical legal rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r14.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن المشهور التفرقة بين الأحكام الأصولية والإعتقادية والأحكام الفرعية العملية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r15.claim: Muslim scholars agree that names and attributes are permitted when authorized by revelation and prohibited when revelation forbids them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r15.anchor: وخلاصة الكلام في هذا المقام أن علماء الإسلام إتفقوا على جواز إطلاق الأسماء والصفات على الباري تعالى إذا ورد بها الأذن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r16.speaker: جمهور أهل الحق
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r16.claim: Where revelation is silent, the majority of the people of truth prohibit praise names that express a true attribute but lack authorization, out of caution.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r16.anchor: فمنعه جمهور أهل الحق مطلقا للخطر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r17.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r17.claim: The Muʿtazila permit such names without restriction when their meanings apply to God and do not imply a deficiency.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r18.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r18.claim: Judge Abu Bakr leaned toward permission because names such as Khuda and Takri were widely used without objection, which he took as consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r18.anchor: ومال إليه القاضي أبوبكر لشيوع إطلاق نحو خدا وتكرى من غير نكير فكان إجماعا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r19.claim: The response is that consensus can supply scriptural authorization if it is actually established.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p120#2/r19.anchor: ورد بأن الإجماع كاف في الأذن الشرعي إذا ثبت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r1.speaker: إمام الحرمين
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r1.claim: He objects that deriving divine names by analogy is invalid because analogy proves practical rulings, whereas names and attributes concern doctrine; some report that he suspended judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r1.anchor: بأنه قول بالقياس وهو حجة في العمليات والأسماء والصفات من العمليات وروى بعضهم عنه التوقف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r2.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r2.claim: Any term denoting a meaning established for God may be used if it does not suggest something unbecoming of Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r2.anchor: أن القاضي أبابكر ذهب إلى أن كل لفظ دل على معنى ثابت لله تعالى جاز إطلاقه عليه إذا لم يكن موهما

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r3.claim: A further qualification proposed is that a term must also signal exaltation after inappropriate implications are excluded.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r3.anchor: لابد مع نفي ذلك الإبهام من الإشعار بالتعظيم حتى يصح الإطلاق بلا توقف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r4.claim: The cited account distinguishes the Qadi's position from the Muʿtazilite position and identifies the previously described view as the well-known one.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r4.anchor: وجعل مذهب المعتزلة غير مذهبه والمشهور ما ذكرناه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r5.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r5.claim: Al-Ghazali permits attributes, which indicate a meaning additional to the essence, but forbids names, which indicate the essence itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r5.anchor: فجوز إطلاق الصفة وهو ما دل على معنى زائد على الذات ومنع إطلاق الإسم وهو ما يدل على نفس الذات

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r6.speaker: الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r6.claim: He argues that truthfulness is permitted and recommended; an attribute makes a predicative assertion and needs only its meaning to be established, unlike a name, which makes no such assertion and is for parents or their equivalents to give.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r6.anchor: محتجا بإباحة الصدق وإستحبابه والصفة لتضمنها النسبة الخبرية راجعة إليه وهي لا تتوقف إلا على تحقق معناها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r7.claim: The reply is that using a term with a predicative relation is permissible only when no bar prevents it; the danger of inappropriate implication remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r7.anchor: وأجيب بأن ذلك حيث لا مانع من إستعمال اللفظ الدال على تلك النسبة والخطر قائم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r8.speaker: جمع من المتأخرين
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r8.claim: They adopt the majority rule: use transmitted names as transmitted, allowing only definiteness or indefiniteness to vary, whether a name might suggest a questionable sense or not.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r8.anchor: واختار جمع من المتأخرين مذهب الجمهور قالوا : فيطلق ما سمع على الوجه الذي سمع ولا يتجاوز ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r9.claim: Transmitted evidence means the Qurʾan, sound Sunnah, or consensus, since consensus in reality derives from one of those sources.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r9.anchor: والمراد بالسمعي ما ورد به كتاب أو سنة صحيحة أو إجماع لأنه غير خارج عنهما في التحقيق

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r10.claim: Depending on whether the issue is classified as practical, some treat a non-severely-weak report like a good report and analogy like consensus; others prohibit analogy, which the author calls the apparent position because synonyms can differ in implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r10.anchor: فالسنة الضعيفة كالحسنة إلا الواهية جدا والقياس كالإجماع وأطلق بعضهم المنع في القياس وهو الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r11.claim: Treating synonyms from one or more languages as names established by analogy is unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r11.anchor: وجعل بعضهم من الثابت بالقياس المترادفات من لغة أو لغات وليس بذاك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r12.claim: Names established by consensus include the Creator, the Existing, the Necessary, and the Eternal; some add the Cause, while others say the Creator and Eternal are transmitted names like al-Ḥannān and al-Mannān.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r12.anchor: ومن الثابت بالإجماع الصانع والموجود والواجب والقديم قيل : والعلة وقيل : الصانع والقديم مسموعان

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r13.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r13.claim: Some authorities forbid an unqualified form when it is an analogical synonym of a transmitted possessive form, and reject terms appearing only figuratively or by wordplay; verbs and verbal nouns alone do not authorize an adjective.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r13.anchor: يمنع إطلاق غير المضاف إذا كان مرادفا للمضاف المسموع قياسا كما يمنع إطلاق ما ورد على وجه المشاكلة والمجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r14.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r14.claim: Thus one may not call God the cultivator, planter, shooter, mocker, sender-down, or schemer merely because verses contain corresponding verbs or verbal forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r14.anchor: فلا يطلق الحارث والزارع والرامي والمستهزيء والمنزل والماكر عليه سبحانه وتعالى وإن جاءت آيات تشعر بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r15.speaker: بعض الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r15.claim: One classification divides terms into three kinds: terms for necessary attributes, terms for impossible attributes, and terms for neither but for established meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r15.anchor: إن الألفاظ الدالة على الصفات ثلاثة أقسام : الأول ما يدل على صفات واجبة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r16.speaker: بعض الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r16.claim: Necessary-attribute terms differ in form: some are used independently, some independently or in a fitting construction, and some only in a construction, such as the reviver of decayed bones.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r16.anchor: منها ما يصح إطلاقه مفردا لا مضافا نحو الموجود والأزلي والقديم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r17.speaker: بعض الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r17.claim: Terms for impossible attributes, such as hand, face, descent, and arrival, may never be applied literally; if revelation uses them, interpretation is required.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r17.anchor: والثاني ما يدل على صفات ممتنعة نحو اليد والوجه والنزول والمجيء فلا يصح إطلاقه البتة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r18.speaker: بعض الناس
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r18.claim: Terms for meanings that are neither necessary nor impossible, such as scheming and deception, are usable only when revelation authorizes them; one must not invoke God as deceiver.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r18.anchor: والثالث ما لايدل على صفات واجبة ولا ممتنعة بل يدل على معان ثابتة نحو المكر والخداع

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r19.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r19.claim: Al-Tibi says invocation must follow authorization: whatever the Lawgiver permits one to invoke God by is a name, whether derived or not; other attributions are descriptions, interpreted or otherwise.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r19.anchor: أن الحق الإعتماد في الإطلاق على الإطلاق على التوقيف وأن كل ما أذن الشارع أن يدعى به الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r20.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r20.claim: Al-Tibi classifies al-Ḥayy as a description and al-Karīm as a name, allowing Ya Karīm but not Ya Ḥayy despite a report containing both terms.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r20.anchor: وجعل الحي وصفا والكريم إسما وادعى أنه يقال يا كريم ولا يقال يا حي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r21.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r21.claim: In a report from Salman cited from Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet says God is Living and Generous and does not turn away a servant's raised hands empty.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r21.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أنه قال : الله تعالى حي كريم يستحي إذا رفع العبد يده أن يردها صفرا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r22.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r22.claim: Al-Tibi takes the definite article in the names to refer to a known set, because the verse commands invocation by them, forbids invocation otherwise, and threatens those who deviate.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r22.anchor: وذكر أن التعريف في الأسماء للعهد وأنه لابد من المعهود لأنه سبحانه وتعالى أمر بالدعاء بها ونهى عن الدعاء بغيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r23.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r23.claim: The Abu Hurayra report says God has ninety-nine names and whoever preserves or enumerates them enters Paradise; its transmitted wordings vary between preserving and enumerating.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r23.anchor: إن لله تسعة وتسعين إسما من حفظها دخل الجنة وفي رواية أحصاها

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r24.claim: A version enumerates the ninety-nine names beginning with Allah, al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, al-Malik, and al-Quddūs; its emphatic total is read as preventing additions to the transmitted count.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r24.anchor: وأوتي فيه بالفذلكة والتأكيد لئلا يزاد على ما ورد وجاءت معدودة في بعض الرويات

ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r25.claim: The author notes that Ahl al-Bayt transmitted a different set drawn from the Qurʾan, and that other reports also differ in some names.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p121/r25.anchor: ونقل عن أهل البيت رضي الله تعالى عنهم غير ذلك وأخذوها من القرآن وجاء أيضا عندنا ما يخالف هذه الرواية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r1.claim: Scholars classify the names as referring to active, essential, or negative attributes, while disagreeing over where Allah belongs; the author says Allah names the essence and is the one to whom all affairs return.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r1.anchor: منها ما يرجع إلى صفة فعلية ومنها ما يرجع إلى صفة نفسية ومنها ما يرجع إلى صفة سلبية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r2.claim: Most scholars regard Allah as the Greatest Name.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r2.anchor: ومن هنا ذهب الجل إلى أنه الإسم الأعظم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r3.claim: Names also differ in exclusivity and in whether they may be invoked alone: Allah and al-Raḥmān are exclusive, while al-Raḥīm and al-Karīm are not; al-Mumīt and al-Ḍārr are paired with life-giving and benefit-giving names.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r3.anchor: وتنقسم قسمة أخرى إلى ما لايجوز إطلاقه على غيره سبحانه وتعالى كالله والرحمن وما يجوز كالرحيم والكريم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r4.claim: The author holds that God's names are not limited to ninety-nine, citing Ibn Masʿud's supplication that invokes every name God named Himself, revealed, taught, or kept in the unseen.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r4.anchor: ويدل على ذلك ما أخرجه البيهقي عن ابن مسعود قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : من أصابه هم أو حزن

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r5.claim: The Ibn Masʿud supplication is explicit that the names are unlimited because it includes names reserved in God's unseen knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r5.anchor: أسألك بكل إسم هو لك سميت به نفسك أو أنزلته في كتابك أو علمته أحدا من خلقك أو إستأثرت به في علم الغيب عندك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r6.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r6.claim: Al-Nawawi reports scholarly consensus that the ninety-nine-name hadith promises Paradise to whoever enumerates that set, without denying other divine names lacking that promise.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r6.anchor: وحكى محيي الدين النووي إتفاق العلماء على ذلك وأن المقصود من الحديث الإخبار بأن هذه التسعة والتسعين من أحصاها دخل الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r7.speaker: أبو بكر ابن العربي
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r7.claim: Ibn al-Arabi transmits estimates of one thousand names, four thousand names, and virtually innumerable names; he considers one thousand a small number.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r7.anchor: ونقل أبوبكر ابن العربي عن بعضهم أن له سبحانه وتعالى ألف إسم ثم قال : وهذا قليل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r8.claim: Some Sufis say God's names can scarcely be counted.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r8.anchor: وعن بعض الصوفية أنها لا تكاد تحصى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r9.claim: The author permits derived names referring to essential or active attributes and negative attributes without a specific transmitted authorization, provided one investigates fully and guards against even the slightest suggestion of imperfection.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r9.anchor: والمختار عندي عدم توقف آطلاق الأسماء المشتقة الراجعة إلى نوع من الصفات النفسية والفعلية وكذا الصفات السلبية عليه تعالى على التوقيف الخاص

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r10.claim: Because people are authorized to glorify God without a prescribed limit, any sufficiently reverential wording is permitted within one's capacity, in keeping with the principle that God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r10.anchor: لأنا مأذونون بتعظيم الله تبارك وتعالى بالأقوال والأفعال ولم يحد لنا حد فيه فمتى كان في الإطلاق تعظيم له

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r11.claim: The caution argument would permit only names whose attribution is mass-transmitted or agreed upon, since other evidence is probabilistic while the danger is certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r11.anchor: حديث الخطر الذي يذكرونه يستدعي أن لايصح إلا إطلاق ما ثبت تواترا إطلاقه عليه جل وعلا أو إجتمعت الأمة على إطلاقه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r12.claim: The familiar Tirmidhi list is absent from many narrations; Tirmidhi says several people related it from Ṣafwān b. Ṣāliḥ and that he knows it only through him, though Ṣafwān is reliable.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r12.anchor: والأسماء المتقدمة آنفا لم يوجد في كثير من الروايات ذكرها وهي مشهورة من حديث الترمذي وقد قال : إنه حدثنا به غير واحد عن صفوان بن صالح

ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r13.claim: The author says this evidence does not establish certainty, and Ahl al-Bayt's enumeration and other lists differ from the famous list.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p123/r13.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن هذا القدر لا يثبت به اليقين بل ولا يمثله ومثله على أن عد بعض أهل البيت

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r1.claim: One could claim consensus on the Tirmidhi list alone, not the conflicting lists, but the author has found no scholar reporting such consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r1.anchor: حصل الإجماع على ما في حديث الترمذي دون ما في حديث غيره المخالف له لكن لم أقف على من حكى ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r2.claim: The names under discussion may be invoked and used as reports or descriptions of God; they are beautiful because their intended meanings, as applied to God, belong to Him uniquely.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r2.anchor: لا مانع من الدعاء بها ومن إجرائها إخبارا عنه سبحانه وتعالى أو أوصافا له جل وعز وكلها حسنى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r3.claim: Divine names do not share their intended meanings with creaturely uses; creaturely words may overlap only in broad features, as black and white share being colors without resembling each other.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r3.anchor: ولا تطلق على غيره بالمعنى المراد منها حال إطلاقها على الله تعالى وإنما تطلق على الغير بمعنى آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r4.claim: God's reality is known only to God; created knowledge of an attribute does not disclose its divine reality, and the highest human knowledge recognizes its own inability to know Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r4.anchor: وكذا هي مفقودة بين العلم مثلا الذي يوصف الله تعالى كما لا يعرف حقيقة الله تعالى إلا الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r5.claim: When a knower realizes that creatures cannot know God in His reality, that recognition itself is the fullest knowledge available to them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r5.anchor: فإذا إنكشف لهم ذلك فقد عرفوا وبلغوا المنتهى الذي يمكن في حق الخلق من معرفته سبحانه وتعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r6.claim: Al-Ṣiddīq al-Akbar expresses this as the incapacity to grasp understanding being understanding itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r6.anchor: حيث قال : العجز عن درك الإدراك إدراك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r7.claim: The Prophet's words, I cannot enumerate praise of You; You are as You praised Yourself, mean that only God encompasses His own praises and divine attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r7.anchor: لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك فإنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أراد إني لا أحيط بمحامدك وصفات إلهيتك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r8.claim: Prophets, angels, and saints differ in knowledge through what they witness of God's signs in the heavens, earth, spirits, and bodies, and thus differ in knowledge of names and attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r8.anchor: وتفاوت درجات الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام والملائكة والأولياء في المعرفة إنما هو بالوقوف على عجائب آياته في ملكوت السموات والأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r9.claim: Knowing that Zayd is learned is not the same as knowing the details of all his knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r9.anchor: ومعرفة أن زيدا عالم مثلا ليست كمعرفة تفاصيل علومه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r10.claim: The distinction between exclusive and nonexclusive names concerns whether their primary meaning prevents application to another; al-Bayḍāwī says al-Raḥmān means the true benefactor whose mercy reaches its limit, which applies only to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r10.anchor: وقد نص البيضاوي على أن معنى الرحمن المنعم الحقيقي البالغ في الرحمة غايتها وذلك لا يصدق على غيره تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r11.claim: A nonexclusive name such as al-Raḥīm has a general meaning applicable to God and others, but when applied to God it denotes the fullest perfection that can belong only to Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r11.anchor: وبغير المختص ما لم يعتبر في مفهومه ذلك بل أعتبر فيه معنى عام فيطلق لذلك على الله تعالى وعلى غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r12.claim: Another account says all derived names whose roots appear in creatures become exclusive when perfection is intended; classifications differ because of usage and the Lawgiver's authorization.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r12.anchor: لا فرق بين الأسماء المشتقة التي يوجد في الغير مبدأ إشتقاقها في الجملة من حيث أن إعتبار ذلك الوجود يقتضي عدم الإختصاص

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r13.claim: If the verse's fronted phrase restricts the names to God alone, reading the names themselves as exclusive makes the restriction tautological; one solution reads them as attributes, perfect in every respect and therefore God's alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r13.anchor: بناء على أن تقديم الخبر يفيد الإختصاص أيضا فيكون المعنى لله لا لغيره الأسماء التي تختص به تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r14.claim: On that reading, invoke God by names derived from His perfect attributes, and leave those who deviate in His attributes by applying names to others or supplicating as though they share divinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r14.anchor: ومعنى فادعوه بها الخ سموه بما يشتق منها أو نادوه بذلك وذروا الذين يميلون عن الحق في صفاته

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r15.claim: The author calls al-Tibi's claim that the names' definite article requires a known set an awkward argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r15.anchor: وما ذكره الطيبي من أن التعريف في الأسماء للعهد إلى آخر ما قاله مما لا أظنك في مرية من ركاكته

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r16.claim: One interpretation takes deviation to mean refusing some of God's names, as when opponents said they knew only the Rahman of Yamama; the command means to avoid omitting any of His names.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r16.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالإلحاد العدول عن تسميته تعالى ببعض أسمائه الكريمة كما قالوا : وما الرحمن إنا لا نعرف إلا رحمن اليمامة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r17.claim: Another interpretation is applying divine names to idols and deriving names such as al-Lāt from Allah and al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz; the command then means to disregard them and await their punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p124/r17.anchor: وأن يراد به إطلاقها على الأصنام وإشتقاق أسمائها منها كاللات من الله تعالى والعزى من العزيز

ALUSI-FULL:v9p125/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p125/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p125/r1.claim: The promise of recompense is a resumed answer to the implied question of why believers should disregard the deviators: punishment will soon arrive, and avoiding their practice keeps it from reaching them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p125/r1.anchor: فإنه إستئناف وقع جوابا عن سؤال مقدر كأنه قيل : لم لا نبالي فقيل : لأنه سينزل بهم عقوبة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.claim: Maqātil says the verse was revealed after a man prayed, invoking both Allah and al-Raḥmān; Meccan polytheists objected that Muḥammad’s followers claimed one God but called two, so God affirmed His beautiful names.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: وذلك أن رجلا دعا الله في صلاته ودعا الرحمن، فقال بعض مشركي مكة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine form of al-aḥsan, like al-kubrā and al-ṣughrā; God is to be invoked by these names.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r2.anchor: والحسنى تأنيث الأحسن كالكبرى والصغرى، فادعوه بها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.claim: The Prophet said God has ninety-nine names, one fewer than a hundred; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise, for God is One and loves what is odd.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p306#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما، مائة إلا واحدا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r1.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads yalḥadūn with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ wherever it occurs; al-Kisāʾī agrees in Sūrat al-Naḥl, while the rest read yulḥidūn with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة: "يلحدون" -بفتح الياء والحاء حيث كان -وافقه الكسائي في النحل، والباقون بضم الياء وكسر الحاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r2.claim: Ilḥād means turning away from the intended course; alhada and lahada both mean to deviate, and this is the form read by Ḥamza.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r2.anchor: ومعنى الإلحاد هو: الميل عن [المقصد] (2) يقال: ألحد يلحد إلحادا، ولحد يلحد لحودا: إذا مال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r3.speaker: يعقوب بن السكيت
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sikkīt defines ilḥād as departing from truth and inserting into it what does not belong.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r3.anchor: قال يعقوب بن السكيت: الإلحاد هو العدول عن الحق، وإدخال ما ليس منه فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r4.claim: They identify those who deviate in God’s names as polytheists who redirect His names to idols, adding or subtracting: al-Lāt from Allah, al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz, and Manāt from al-Mannān.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r4.anchor: وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} هم المشركون عدلوا بأسماء الله تعالى عما هي عليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r5.claim: Another view says they called idols gods.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
