BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r6.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās interprets ilḥād in God’s names as lying.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r6.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: يلحدون في أسمائه أي يكذبون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r7.claim: The scholars of meaning say ilḥād includes assigning God a name not found in the Qurʾān or the Prophet’s Sunna.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r7.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: الإلحاد في أسماء الله: تسميته بما لم يسم به، ولم ينطق به كتاب الله ولا سنة رسول الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r8.claim: God’s names are fixed by transmitted authority: one may call Him Jawād, Raḥīm, and ʿĀlim, but not the synonymous Sakhi, Rafīq, or ʿĀqil.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r8.anchor: وجملته: أن أسماء الله تعالى على التوقيف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r9.claim: Although the Qurʾān predicates deception and plotting of God, one must not use ‘deceiver’ or ‘plotter’ as invocations; invoke only transmitted names reverently.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r9.anchor: ولا يقال في الدعاء: يا مخادع، يا مكار، بل يدعى بأسمائه التي ورد بها التوقيف على وجه التعظيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r10.claim: Those who deviate in God’s names will be repaid in the hereafter for their deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p307/r10.anchor: سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون} في الآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r1.claim: God's names are beautiful because they signify the best meanings; the phrase may mean the names as words or, alternatively, the attributes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r1.anchor: لأنها دالة على معان هي أحسن المعاني

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r2.claim: Invoke God by those names, that is, call Him by them.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r3.claim: One interpretation is to leave those who invent unsanctioned divine names that could suggest a corrupt meaning, such as calling Him Father of Generosities or White of Face.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r3.anchor: الذين يسمونه بما لا توقيف فيه، إذ ربما يوهم معنى فاسدا

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r4.claim: Another interpretation is not to be troubled by those who deny God's revealed names, claiming they know only the Merciful of Yamāma.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r4.anchor: كقولهم: ما نعرف إلا رحمان اليمامة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r5.claim: A further interpretation is to leave those who apply God's names to idols and derive idol names from them, such as al-Lāt from Allāh and al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz, without agreeing with them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r5.anchor: بإطلاقها على الأصنام واشتقاق أسمائها منها كاللات من «الله»

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r6.claim: Alternatively, leave the deviants and their misnaming alone, since God will recompense them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r6.anchor: أو أعرضوا عنهم فإن الله مجازيهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r7.claim: Ḥamza reads يلحدون with fatḥ here and in Fuṣṣilat; laḥada and alḥada both mean to deviate from the right course.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:180/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة هنا وفي «فصلت» { يلحدون } بالفتح يقال: لحد وألحد إذا مال عن القصد

SULAMI:v1p251/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p251/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p251/r1.claim: Some say each divine name brings the invoker to a spiritual rank: the name Allah to passionate love and the names al-Rahman and al-Rahim to mercy, provided the invocation is sincere.
SULAMI:v1p251/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : كل اسم من أسمائه يبلغك مرتبة من المراتب ، واسم الله يبلغك الوله في حبه

SULAMI:v1p251/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p251/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p251/r2.claim: Some say invoking God by His names means stopping at them without claiming to grasp their reality.
SULAMI:v1p251/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم في هذه الآية ﴿ ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها ﴾ : أي قفوا معها عن إدراك حقيقتها

SULAMI:v1p251/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p251/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p251/r3.claim: Some say realities lie beyond names and attributes, beyond the intellect's reach; the Real is like a blazing fire that cannot be approached without entering it.
SULAMI:v1p251/r3.anchor: وقيل في قوله : ﴿ ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها ﴾ قال : إنه وراء الأسماء أسماء والصفات صفات

SULAMI:v1p251/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p251/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p251/r4.claim: Some say God displayed His names so people could invoke Him through them, not so anyone might claim to comprehend His attributes.
SULAMI:v1p251/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أبدى أسماءه للدعاء لا بطلب الوقوف عليها ، وأنى يقف على صفاته أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r2.claim: After describing people as misguided, the author prevents the inference that God is unworthy: only God possesses every beautiful name and attribute of perfection, free of deficiency and temporal change.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r2.anchor: { الأسماء } ولما كان الاسم إذالحظت فيه الناسبه كان بمعنى الصفة , أنث في قوله { الحسنى } أي كلها باتصافه دون غيره بصفات الكمال

BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r3.claim: The author argues from contingency: changing created things are possible and need a chooser to prefer existence; this establishes God's free choice and power, then wisdom, knowledge, life, hearing, sight, speech, will, and unity, since otherwise disorder would follow.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r3.anchor: كل ممكن محتاج وأدنى ما يحتاج إلى مرجح يرجح وجوده

BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r4.claim: Call on God through His names by describing, naming, and asking Him with them; remembrance frees the heart from worldly desire and affliction, and God's many names display the greatness of their bearer without compromising oneness.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r4.anchor: { فادعوه } أي فصفوه وسموه واسألوه { بها } لتنجوا من جهنم وتنالوا كل ما تحمد عاقبته

BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r5.claim: Those who deviate in God's names either assign them to others, thereby implying all divine attributes, or use unauthorized names; some are permissible only alongside their complement, while names implying deficiency are forbidden.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r5.anchor: { في أسمائه } أي فيطلقونها على غيره بأن يسموه إلها , فليزمهم أن يطلقوا عليه جميع أوصاف الإله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r6.claim: Examples of illicit naming include calling God father or body, using a derivative like 'teacher' merely because He is knowing, naming Him with a term suggesting deficient creatures, or invoking an unknown term despite popular praise.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r6.anchor: مثل إطلاق الأب عليه والجسم , وكذا كل ما أهم نقصا , فلم يكن أحسن

BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān, transmitting from Ibn al-Sikkīt, says the simple and derived forms of the verb both mean deviating from truth and introducing what does not belong to it.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r7.anchor: العدول عن الحق والإدخال فيه ما ليس منه - نقله أبو حيان عن ابن السكيت

BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r8.speaker: الإمام أبو القاسم علي بن جعفر بن القطاع
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r8.claim: Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ's lexicon gives laḥada as making a lateral grave niche and as inclining toward, away from, or within religion; both forms are read accordingly.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r8.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو القاسم علي بن جعفر بن القطاع في كتاب الأفعال : لحد الميت لحدا وألحده

BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r9.claim: The passive 'they will be recompensed' emphasizes that the warning is about the occurrence of retribution, not who inflicts it; it applies in this world and the next, as an unfailing promise.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r9.anchor: وكان المرهب إيقاع الجزاء , لاكونه من معين

BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r10.claim: Their punishment corresponds to their habitual acts; after describing those destined for Hell, the author transitions to the remaining group among God's creation, introduced in 7:181.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p159/r10.anchor: ولما أخبر تعالى عن ذرء جهنم من القبلتين , تشوف السامع إلى معرفة حال الباقين منهما

TUSTARI:7:180/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:180/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:180/r1.claim: Beyond the names and attributes are qualities beyond intellectual grasp; the Real is a blazing fire inaccessible without plunging into it.
TUSTARI:7:180/r1.anchor: إن وراء الأسامي والصفات صفات لا تخرقها الأفهام، لأن الحق نار يتضرم لا سبيل إليه

TUSTARI:7:180/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:7:180/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:7:180/r2.claim: Those who commit ilhad in God's names wrong them and lie about them.

DURR-FULL:v3p613/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r3.claim: The Prophet says God has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise, for God is One and loves odd numbers.
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحدا

DURR-FULL:v3p613/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet says God has one hundred names minus one and that whoever invokes Him by them has their prayer answered.
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r4.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لله مائة اسم غير اسم من دعا بها استجاب الله له دعاءه

DURR-FULL:v3p613/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r5.claim: A report attributed to God says He has ninety-nine names and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: قال الله عز وجل: لي تسعة وتسعون اسما

DURR-FULL:v3p613/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar transmit the Prophet’s statement that whoever enumerates God’s ninety-nine names enters Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v3p613/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس وابن عمر قالا: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما

DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ilḥād in God’s names means denial.
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: الإلحاد التكذيب

DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the polytheists derived al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz and al-Lāt from Allah.
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} قال: اشتقوا العزى من العزيز

DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r3.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets ilḥād as imitation or resemblance.
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r3.anchor: عن عطاء في الآية قال: الإلحاد الضاهاة

DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r4.speaker: الأعمش
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r4.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads يَلْحَدُونَ with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ, from laḥd, interpreting it as introducing into God’s names what does not belong to them.
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r4.anchor: عن الأعمش أنه قرأ (يلحدون) بنصب الياء والحاء من اللحد

DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r5.claim: Qatāda interprets ilḥād in God’s names as associating partners with Him.
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة {وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} قال: يشركون

DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r6.claim: Qatāda also glosses ilḥād in God’s names as lying about His names.
DURR-FULL:v3p616#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة {يلحدون في أسمائه} قال: يكذبون في أسمائه

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r1.claim: Two reports from Abu Hurayra attribute to the Prophet the promise that whoever enumerates God’s ninety-nine names will enter Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r1.anchor: عن ابى هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ان لله تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة غير واحد من احصاها دخل الجنة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas names al-ʿAziz and al-Jabbar among God’s names and says every divine name is beautiful.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ولله الاسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها قال : ومن اسمائه العزيز والجبار وكل اسماء الله حسن

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses those who distort God’s names as deniers.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : الذين يلحدون في اسمائه التكذيب

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the distortion is calling al-Lat and al-ʿUzza by names of God.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وذروا الذين يلحدون في اسمائه قال : الالحاد ، الملحدين ان دعوا اللات والعزى في اسماء الله عز وجل

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r5.speaker: أبوه
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r5.claim: The report glosses ilhad in God’s signs as distortion through imitation.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r5.anchor: عن أبيه ، واما يلحدون في اياتنا قال : الالحاد المضاهاة

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r6.claim: Qatada glosses distorting God’s names as associating partners with Him.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r6.anchor: عن معمر ، عن قتادة قوله يلحدون قال : يشركون

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r7.speaker: الأعمش
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r7.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads the verb with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ, from laḥd, and explains it as inserting into God’s names what does not belong there.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1622/r7.anchor: قال الاعمش : يلحدون بنصب الياء والحاء من اللحد قال : وسالته عن تفسيرها فقال : يدخلون فيها ما ليس منها

AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r1.claim: Some derive يلحدون from لحد يلحد; this and ألحد يلحد are two Arabic dialects, with يلحدون more common and preferred by Akhfash.
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم {يلحدون} جعله من "لحد" [123 ء] "يلحد" وهي لغة.

AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r2.claim: Akhfash prefers the more common reading يلحدون; ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم supports this form.
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r2.anchor: وهما لغتان و {يلحدون} أكثر وبها نقرأ ويقويها {ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد بظلم}

AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r3.claim: In حملت حملا خفيفا, ḥaml with fatḥa is pregnancy in the womb, while ḥiml with kasra is a load carried on the back.
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r3.anchor: وقال {حملت حملا خفيفا} لأن "الحمل" ما كان في الجوف و"الحمل" ما كان على الظهر

AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r4.claim: أثقلت means she became one bearing weight, like أتمرنا meaning we became possessors of dates, ألبنا of milk, and the earth's becoming grassy or producing truffles.
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r4.anchor: وأما قوله {أثقلت} فيقول: "صارت ذات ثقل" كما تقول "أتمرنا" أي: "صرنا ذوي تمر" و"ألبنا"

AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p342#2/r5.claim: Some also read فلما أثقلت, the same form as in the base text but a reported vocalized reading.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r1.claim: This address to Muslims interrupts the condemnation of polytheists because shirk is their worst trait: it denies divine oneness and related attributes, disables other divine qualities, and their defiance led them to deny the name al-Rahman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r1.anchor: لأن في ذلك إبطالا لأخص الصفات بمعنى الإلهية : وهي صفة الوحدانية وما في معناها من الصفات نحو الفرد ، الصمد .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r2.claim: After describing their idolatrous error, the passage tells Muslims to invoke God by names that express his divine attributes, persist in this, and ignore the polytheists’ objections.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r2.anchor: فعقبت الآيات التي وصفت ضلال إشراكهم بتنبيه المسلمين للاقبال على دعاء الله بأسمائه الدالة على عظيم صفات الإلهية ، والدوام على ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r3.speaker: ابن عطية وغيره
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya and others report that Abu Jahl heard a Companion recite Allah and then al-Rahman, and objected that Muhammad claimed one god while worshipping many; the verse was revealed in response. The mockery came from contrarianism, not ignorance of God’s mercy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r3.anchor: أنه روي في سبب نزول قوله تعالى : { ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها } أن أبا جهل سمع بعض أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ فيذكر الله في قراءته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r4.claim: The verse is connected to the preceding account as further news about polytheist error; its purpose is the command to leave those who deviate from God’s names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r4.anchor: فعطف هذه الآية على التي قبلها عطف الإخبار عن أحوال المشركين وضلالهم ، والغرض منها قوله : { وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه } .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r5.claim: Fronting the predicate لِلَّهِ gives emphasis and confirms that God deserves these names; this prepares the command to invoke him and counters the claim that multiple names mean multiple gods, as in 17:110, 20:8, and 59:24.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p185/r5.anchor: وتقديم المجرور المسند على المسند إليه ؛ لمجرد الاهتمام المفيد تأكيد استحقاقه إياها ، المستفاد من اللام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r1.claim: A divine name is a word made a designation of the essence by specific naming or common usage: Allah is specific, while al-Rahman, al-Rahim, and attribute words used as names are conventional; genitive compounds such as ذو الجلال are descriptive instead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r1.anchor: والأسماء هي الألفاظ المجعولة أعلاما على الذات بالتخصيص أو بالغلبة فاسم الجلالة وهو ( الله ) علم على ذات الإله الحق بالتخصيص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r2.claim: Al-husna is the feminine of al-ahsan, denoting perfect intrinsic beauty recognized by sound minds free of whim, not mere suitability to each person’s preferences.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r2.anchor: والحسنى مؤنث الأحسن ، وهو المتصف بالحسن الكامل في ذاته ، المقبول لدى العقول السليمة المجردة عن الهوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r3.claim: The names are beautiful because they denote real perfection: some qualities belong perfectly only to God, while traits like al-Mutakabbir and al-Jabbar are blameworthy in needy creatures but a source of justice and right judgment in the absolutely self-sufficient Creator.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r3.anchor: ووصف الأسماء ب { الحسنى } : لأنها دالة على ثبوت صفات كمال حقيقي ، أما بعضها فلأن معانيها الكاملة لم تثبت إلا لله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r4.claim: Calling God by these names follows from their belonging to one named essence and their beauty; the verse thus permits invoking God by any name that denotes his attributes or acts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r4.anchor: أي فلا حرج في دعائه بها ؛ لأنها أسماء متعددة لمسمى واحد ، لا كما يزعم المشركون ، ولأنها حسنى فلا ضير في دعاء الله تعالى بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r5.claim: A term for a divine attribute or act may be used as a name when conventionally intelligible, except if it is figurative (as in 2:15) or ordinarily suggests a defect, as in “plotter” from 3:54.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p186/r5.anchor: وقد دلت الآية على أن كل ما دل على صفة الله تعالى وشأن من شؤونه على وجه التقريب للأفهام بحسب المعتاد يسوغ أن يطلق منه اسم لله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports disagreement over applying a pure, unambiguous term of praise not established in revelation as a divine name: al-Baqillani permits it, while Abu al-Hasan al-Ashari, jurists, and the majority forbid it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r1.anchor: واختلف في الاسم الذي يقتضي مدحا خالصا ، ولا تتعلق به شبهة ولا اشتراك إلا أنه لم يرد منصوصا هل يطلق ويسمى الله به ، فنص الباقلاني على جواز ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers restricting divine names to those used by revelation, since few can judge a name free of ambiguity and nonexperts might admit names that are unanimously improper.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r2.anchor: والصواب : أن لا يسمى الله تعالى إلا باسم قد أطلقته الشريعة ، وأن يكون مدحا خالصا لا شبهة فيه ولا اشتراك أمر لا يحسنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r3.claim: One group says Qur'anic verbs such as God mocking people or plotting should never be turned into divine names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r3.anchor: واختلف في الأفعال التي في القرآن نحو { الله يستهزىء بهم } ( البقرة : 15 ) و { مكر الله } ( آل عمران : 54 ) ونحو ذلك هل يطلق منها اسم الفاعل ، فقالت فرقة : لا يطلق ذلك بوجه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r4.speaker: فرقة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r4.claim: Another group allows the active name only when qualified by its cause, such as God plotting against those who plot against religion; unqualified use is unanimously forbidden.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r4.anchor: وجوزت فرقة أن يقال ذلك مقيدا بسببه نحو : الله ماكر بالذين يمكرون بالدين ، وأما إطلاق ذلك دون تقييد فممنوع إجماعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r5.claim: Leaving those who deviate means stopping prolonged debate because they do not seek truth, or refusing to hear them lest their doubts mislead ordinary believers; God will requite them. The verb dhar was explained at 6:70.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r5.anchor: والمراد من ترك { الذين يلحدون في أسمائه } الإمساك عن الاسترسال في محاجتهم لظهور أنهم غير قاصدين معرفة الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r6.claim: Ilhad means turning from the middle of something to its side; by analogy, deviation from truth to falsehood is called ilhad, applied to disbelief and corruption, usually deliberate, and the form ألحد is more common than لحد.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r6.anchor: والإلحاد : الميل عن وسط الشيء إلى جانبه ، وإلى هذا المعنى ترجع مشتقاته كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r7.claim: All readers except Hamza read يلحدون with a yāʾ in ḍamma and ḥāʾ in kasra from the hamzated form; Hamza alone opens both vowels from the unhamzated form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p188/r7.anchor: وقرأ من عدا حمزة يلحدون } بضم الياء وكسر الحاء من ألحد المهموز ، وقرأه حمزة وحده : بفتح الياء والحاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r1.claim: The possessive phrase God’s names indicates the names for which revelation provides grounds for naming him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r1.anchor: وإضافة الأسماء إلى الله تؤذن بأن المقصود أسماؤه التي ورد في الشرع ما يقتضي تسميته بها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r2.claim: Deviating in God’s names means turning them into an avenue of disbelief by denying names for attributes truly established in him, especially al-Rahman, and weaponizing its Quranic use to mock the Prophet as claiming many gods; this is deliberate, envious distortion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r2.anchor: ومعنى الإلحاد في أسماء الله جعلها مظهرا من مظاهر الكفر ، وذلك بإنكار تسميته تعالى بالأسماء الدالة على صفات ثابتة له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r3.claim: He reads في أسمائه causally, as in the prophetic report about a woman entering Hell because of a cat and Ibn Abi Rabiʿa’s verse about acting because of a beloved.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r3.anchor: وهذا يناسب أن يكون حرف ( في ) من قوله : { في أسمائه } مستعملا في معنى التعليل كقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( دخلت امرأة النار في هرة ) الحديث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r4.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r4.claim: The commentators mention three other explanations of deviation in God’s names, including al-Fakhr’s; Ibn Ashur rejects them as incompatible with the possessive link to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r4.anchor: وقد جوز المفسرون احتمالات أخرى في معنى الإلحاد في أسمائه : منها ثلاثة ذكرها الفخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r5.claim: The promise of recompense explains the command to leave the deviants and consoles believers; the general relative ما includes all their disbelief, including their deviation in the names, which is called work because it proceeds from hearts and tongues.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r5.anchor: وجملة : { سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون } تتنزل منزلة التعليل للأمر بترك الملحدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r6.claim: The future particle سين confirms the coming recompense, and saying ما كانوا يعملون marks their conduct as a persistent, renewed practice rather than a single act.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p189/r6.anchor: وقيل : { ما كانوا يعملون } دون ما عملوا أو ما يعملون للدلالة على أن ذلك العمل سنة لهم ومتجدد منهم .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r1.claim: A reported occasion says Abu Jahl heard the Prophet’s companions invoke Allah and al-Rahman in recitation, objected that Muhammad claimed one god while worshipping many, and the verse was revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r1.anchor: أن أبا جهل سمع بعض أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ فيذكر الله في قراءته ومرة يقرأ فيذكر الرحمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r2.claim: The exegetes agree that al-asmāʾ here means names or designations, with no viable alternative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r2.anchor: والأسماء هنا بمعنى التسميات إجماعا من المتأولين لا يمكن غيره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r3.claim: Al-ḥusnā is a verbal noun used adjectivally; alternatively it is the feminine of aḥsan, with one adjective used for a nonrational plural, as in the cited examples.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r3.anchor: والحسنى: مصدر وصف به، ويجوز أن تقدر الحسنى فعلى مؤنثه أحسن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r4.claim: The names’ goodness comes from the law authorizing and specifying their use, and also from the noble, beautiful meanings they contain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r4.anchor: وحسن الأسماء إنما يتوجه بتحسين الشرع لإطلاقها، والنص عليها، وانضاف إلى ذلك أيضا أنها إنما تضمنت معاني حسانا شريفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r5.speaker: ابن الباقلاني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r5.claim: Ibn al-Baqillani permits applying to God an untransmitted name that entails pure praise and has no ambiguity or association.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r5.anchor: فنص ابن الباقلاني على جواز ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r6.claim: Abu al-Hasan al-Ashʿari forbids applying such an untransmitted name to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r6.anchor: ونص أبو الحسن الأشعري على منع ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r7.speaker: الفقهاء والجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r7.claim: The jurists and majority also forbid untransmitted names; Ibn ʿAtiyya prefers restricting divine names to those established by revelation, since judging pure praise without ambiguity requires rare expertise and could lead people to invent forbidden names.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r7.anchor: والفقهاء والجمهور على المنع، وهو الصواب أن لا يسمى الله تعالى إلا باسم قد أطلقته الشريعة ووقفت عليه أيضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r8.claim: One group says no agent name may be derived from Qurʾanic acts such as God mocking or plotting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r8.anchor: فقالت فرقة: لا يطلق ذلك بوجه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r9.claim: Another group permits derived names only when qualified by their cause, such as “mocking the disbelievers” or “plotting against those who plot against religion.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r9.anchor: وجوزت فرقة أن يقال ذلك مقيدا بسببه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r10.claim: Unqualified use of such derived names is unanimously forbidden; Ibn ʿAtiyya prefers the first view because the Qurʾanic verb form suffices and no need compels the qualified alternative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r10.anchor: وأما إطلاق ذلك دون تقييد فممنوع إجماعا، والقول الأول أقوى ولا ضرورة تدفع إلى القول الثاني

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r11.claim: Divine names include those in the Qurʾan and those in mutawatir hadith; these are the sources one should rely on.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r11.anchor: ومنها ما ورد في الحديث وتواتر، وهذا هو الذي ينبغي أن يعتمد عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r12.claim: The Tirmidhi report from Abu Hurayra lists ninety-nine names, some of which are anomalous; it is not mutawatir. The mutawatir wording is that whoever enumerates God’s ninety-nine names enters Paradise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r12.anchor: وقد ورد في الترمذي حديث عن أبي هريرة ونص فيه تسعة وتسعين اسما، وفي بعضها شذوذ وذلك الحديث ليس بالمتواتر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r13.claim: Enumerating the names means counting and memorizing them, believing in them, revering them, aspiring through them, and reflecting on their meanings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r13.anchor: ومعنى أحصاها عدها وحفظها وتضمن ذلك الإيمان بها والتعظيم لها والرغبة فيها والعبرة في معانيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r14.claim: A prophetic supplication includes the names “O Ḥannān, O Mannān,” which do not occur in al-Tirmidhi’s list.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p480/r14.anchor: «يا حنان يا منان» ولم يقع هذان الاسمان في تسمية الترمذي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r1.claim: “Call upon Him by them” grants permission to invoke God using these names.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd takes “leave those” to mean leave them without arguing or confronting them; on this interpretation the verse was abrogated by fighting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد: معناه اتركوهم ولا تحاجوهم ولا تعرضوا لهم، فالآية على هذا منسوخة بالقتال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes the wording as a threat, comparable to the cited commands to leave the guilty to eat and enjoy themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه الوعيد كقوله تعالى: ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r4.claim: Alhada and lahada both mean to deviate, incline, or turn aside; alhada is more common, and the author cites an anonymous line using al-mulḥid.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r4.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: [الرجز] ليس الإمام بالشحيح الملحد قال أبو علي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r5.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r5.claim: Abu ʿAli says the form under discussion is scarcely heard in usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r5.anchor: قال أبو علي: ولا يكاد يسمع لأحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r6.claim: The author connects the root to the Qurʾanic phrase “with deviation” and to the grave’s sideward niche (laḥd).
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r6.anchor: وفي القرآن ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد [الحج: 25] ومنه لحد القبر المائل إلى أحد شقيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r7.claim: These readers pronounce yalḥidūna with yāʾ ḍamma and ḥāʾ kasra, likewise at the occurrences in al-Naḥl and al-Sajda.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر «يلحدون» بضم الياء وكسر الحاء، وكذلك في النحل والسجدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r8.speaker: حمزة وابن وثاب وطلحة وعيسى والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r8.claim: Hamza reads all three occurrences with yāʾ and ḥāʾ fatḥa; Ibn Waththab, Talha, ʿIsa, and al-Aʿmash do likewise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r8.anchor: وقرأ حمزة الأحرف الثلاثة «يلحدون» بفتح الياء والحاء، وكذلك ابن وثاب وطلحة وعيسى والأعمش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains deviation in God’s names as naming al-Lat as a counterpart to Allah.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r9.anchor: أن يسموا اللات نظيرا إلى اسم الله تعالى قاله ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r10.claim: Mujahid explains the practice as naming al-ʿUzza as a counterpart to al-ʿAziz.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r10.anchor: والعزى نظيرا إلى العزيز، قاله مجاهد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r11.claim: Another form of deviation is calling God “Lord” while calling idols “lords.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r11.anchor: ويسمون الله ربا ويسمون أوثانهم أربابا ونحو هذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r12.claim: The promise that they will be recompensed is an unqualified threat of punishment in the afterlife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r12.anchor: سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون وعيد محض بعذاب الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r13.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r13.claim: Al-Kisaʾi distinguishes alhada as meaning to deviate from lahada as meaning to lean or seek refuge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r13.anchor: وذهب الكسائي إلى الفرق بين ألحد ولحد وزعم أن ألحد بمعنى مال وانحرف ولحد بمعنى ركن وانضوى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r14.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r14.claim: Al-Kisaʾi reads all Qurʾanic occurrences with yāʾ ḍamma and ḥāʾ kasra except al-Naḥl, which he reads with both vowels open as “leaning”; Abu ʿAli transmits the same account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p481/r14.anchor: قال الطبري: وكان الكسائي يقرأ جميع ما في القرآن بضم الياء وكسر الحاء إلا التي في النحل فإنه كان يقرؤها بفتح الياء والحاء

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p175#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p175#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p175#2/r1.claim: Examples of God's beautiful names are al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, and al-ʿAzīz.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p175#2/r1.anchor: أي: الرحمن والرحيم والعزيز. وأشباه ذلك

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p175#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p175#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p175#2/r2.claim: Ilḥād in God's names is deviation from truth, such as calling idols al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt; laḥd is named for a grave's side.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p175#2/r2.anchor: أي: يجورون عن الحق ويعدلون. فيقولون: اللات والعزى ومناة، وأشباه ذلك.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r1.claim: Mujahid reports that a man called on God in prayer using both Allah and al-Rahman; Abu Jahl objected that Muhammad's followers claim one Lord, so God revealed this verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r1.anchor: أن رجلا دعا الله في صلاته ودعا الرحمن فقال أبو جهل أليس يزعم محمد وأصحابه أنهم يعبدون ربا واحدا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r2.claim: Al-husna is the feminine superlative: all God's names are beautiful, not merely some of them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r2.anchor: فأما الحسنى فهي تأنيث الأحسن ومعنى الآية أن أسماء الله حسنى وليس المراد أن فيها ما ليس بحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r3.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi says the intended names are those people favor invoking for mercy and forgiveness rather than wrath and vengeance.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r3.anchor: وذكر الماوردي أن المراد بذلك ما مالت إليه النفوس من ذكره بالعفو والرحمة دون السخط والنقمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r4.claim: Calling God by these names means invoking Him with names such as Allah and al-Rahman.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r4.anchor: أي نادوه بها كقولك يا الله يا رحمن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, Asim, and Ibn Amir read yulhidun with a damma on ya, including in al-Nahl and al-Sajda; Hamza reads with fatha, joined by al-Kisai and Khalaf in al-Nahl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وعاصم وابن عامر يلحدون بضم الياء وكذلك في النحل والسجدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r6.speaker: الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash says alhada and lahada are two dialect forms; the readings use each form, and ilhad is deviation from the straight path.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r6.anchor: قال الأخفش ألحد ولحد لغتان فمن قرأ بهما أراد الأخذ باللغتين فكأن الإلحاد العدول عن الاستقامة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the idolaters deviate from truth by naming idols al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة يجورون عن الحق ويعدلون فيقولون اللات والعزى ومناة وأشباه ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says one should invoke God only by names He gave Himself, not by unreported names such as generous, lavish, strong, or amiable.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r8.anchor: قال الزجاج ولا ينبغي لأحد أن يدعوه بما لم يسم به نفسه فيقول يا جواد ولا يقول يا سخي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r9.speaker: أبو سليمان الخطابي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r9.claim: Al-Khattabi treats error in God's names as ilhad and criticizes popular, unsupported formulas such as 'Ya Subhan' and 'Ya Burhan' or 'Lord of Ta Ha and Ya Sin'; Ibn Abbas also rejected 'Lord of the Quran.'
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r9.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الخطابي ودليل هذه الآية أن الغلط في أسمائه والزيغ عنها إلحاد ومما يسمع على ألسنة العامة قولهم يا سبحان يا برهان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says idolaters named their idols after God's names and altered them: al-Lat from Allah, al-Uzza from al-Aziz, and Manat from al-Mannan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p292#2/r10.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن إلحادهم في أسمائه أنهم سموا بها أوثانهم وزادوا فيها ونقصوا منها فاشتقوا اللات من الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p293/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p293/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p293/r1.claim: The majority say the verse remains operative because it is phrased as a threat, like the command to leave the one created alone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p293/r1.anchor: والجمهور على أن هذه الآية محكمة لأنها خارجة مخرج التهديد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p293/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p293/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p293/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says it was abrogated by the fighting verse, since leaving those who deviate in God's names implies turning away from unbelievers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p293/r2.anchor: الإعراض عن الكفار وهذا قول ابن زيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p514#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p514#2/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p514#2/r1.claim: The Prophet reports that God has ninety-nine names, one short of one hundred; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise, and God is One and loves odd numbers. Ibn Kathir cites both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p514#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن لله تسعا وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p514#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p514#2/r2.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p514#2/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhī transmits a version that appends a list of divine names; he calls the report unusual and says the names appear in few transmissions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p514#2/r2.anchor: ثم قال الترمذي: هذا حديث غريب وقد روي من غير وجه عن أبي هريرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir follows hadith specialists who regard the enumerated list as an insertion: scholars gathered the names from the Qur'an, as reportedly said by Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, and Abū Zayd al-Lughawī.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r1.anchor: والذي عول عليه جماعة من الحفاظ أن سرد الأسماء في هذا الحديث مدرج فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r2.claim: God's beautiful names are not limited to ninety-nine: Ibn Kathir cites Ibn Masʿūd's supplication asking by every name God named, taught, revealed, or kept in unseen knowledge, after which God removes distress and replaces it with joy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "ما أصاب أحدا قط هم ولا حزن فقال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r3.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says some scholars compiled one thousand divine names from the Qur'an and Sunnah; Ibn Kathir leaves the matter to God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r3.anchor: أبو بكر بن العربي أحد أئمة المالكية في كتابه: "الأحوذي في شرح الترمذي"؛ أن بعضهم جمع من الكتاب والسنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r4.claim: Al-ʿAwfī transmits Ibn ʿAbbās's view that associating al-Lāt with God's names is a form of illicit deviation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r4.anchor: وقال العوفي عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى: {وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} قال: إلحاد الملحدين: أن دعوا "اللات (11) في أسماء الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the polytheists derived al-Lāt from Allah and al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جريج، عن مجاهد: {وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} قال: اشتقوا "اللات" من الله، واشتقوا "العزى" من العزيز

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r6.claim: Qatādah interprets illicit deviation in God's names as associating partners with Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: {يلحدون} يشركون. وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r7.claim: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah reports Ibn ʿAbbās's interpretation of illicit deviation as denial.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r7.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: الإلحاد: التكذيب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r8.claim: In Arabic, illicit deviation means turning from the right course, inclining, injustice, or straying; a burial niche is called laḥd because it angles toward the qibla from the grave's line.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p515/r8.anchor: وأصل الإلحاد في كلام العرب: العدل عن القصد، والميل والجور والانحراف، ومنه اللحد في القبر، لانحرافه إلى جهة القبلة عن سمت الحفر

JISHUMI:v4p2787/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r3.speaker: حمزة والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r3.claim: These readers use the open-yāʾ and open-ḥāʾ form yalḥadūna here and in the cited passages; al-Kisāʾī agrees in al-Naḥl.
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة والأعمش ويحيى بن وثاب يلحدون بفتح الياء والحاء هاهنا، وفي (النحل)

JISHUMI:v4p2787/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r4.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī also reads the open form in al-Naḥl.

JISHUMI:v4p2787/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r5.claim: The other readers use the closed-yāʾ, kasra-ḥāʾ form; both forms are valid Arabic and mean deviation from the truth.
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r5.anchor: والباقون جميع ذلك بضم الياء وكسر الحاء وهما لغتان صحيحتان

JISHUMI:v4p2787/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r6.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r6.claim: Al-Kisāʾī distinguishes ilḥād from luḥūd and takes the al-Naḥl usage to mean inclination or reliance.
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r6.anchor: فأما الكسائي فكان يفرق بين الإلحاد واللحود، ويقول: التي في (النحل) بمعنى الركون

JISHUMI:v4p2787/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r7.speaker: الأحمر
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r7.claim: Al-Aḥmar says laḥadt means to deviate, while alḥadt means to argue or dispute, citing the phrase about a foreign tongue.
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r7.anchor: وقال الأحمر: لحدت: جرت وملت، وألحدت: جادلت وماريت

JISHUMI:v4p2787/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r9.claim: An “ism” signifies a meaning without being bound to time; some names describe an attribute such as power or knowledge, while others are pure titles, and ḥusnā is the feminine of ḥasan.
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r9.anchor: والاسم ما دل على معنى غير مقرون بزمان، ثم ينقسم، فمنه ما يفيد صفة في المسمى كقولنا: قادر عالم

JISHUMI:v4p2787/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r10.claim: Ilḥād is departing from the intended course, originally meaning to incline; laḥd is the side niche in a grave, and the related grave terms name the same feature.
JISHUMI:v4p2787/r10.anchor: والإلحاد: العدول عن القصد، وأصله الميل، ومنه: لحد القبر

NAHHAS:v2p163/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p163/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p163/r13.claim: The Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, and al-Kisāʾī use the first reading; Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, and Ḥamza read yalḥadūn with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ.
NAHHAS:v2p163/r13.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل المدينة وأبي عمرو وعاصم والكسائي وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة ( يلحدون ) بفتح الياء والحاء

NAHHAS:v2p163/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p163/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p163/r14.claim: The eloquent forms are alḥada in religion and laḥada for a grave; either may replace the other because both express inclination.
NAHHAS:v2p163/r14.anchor: واللغة الفصيحة ألحد في دينه ولحد القبر وقد تدخل كل واحدة منهما على الأخرى لأن المعنى معنى الميل

NAHHAS:v2p163/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p163/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p163/r15.claim: Ilḥād in God's names means either assigning divinity to another or naming God by names other than His own.
NAHHAS:v2p163/r15.anchor: ومعنى يلحدون في أسمائه على ضربين أحدهما أن يسموا غيره إلها والآخر أن يسموه بغير أسمائه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r1.claim: God's names are the most beautiful because they express good meanings such as glorification and sanctification, and He should be invoked by them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r1.anchor: التي هي أحسن الأسماء ؛ لأنها تدل على معان حسنة من تمجيد وتقديس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r2.claim: Those who deviate in the names either call God by impermissible labels, as ignorant Bedouins do, or refuse one of His beautiful names, such as al-Raḥmān.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r2.anchor: كما سمعنا البدو يقولون بجهلهم : يا أبا المكارم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the verse means God's beautiful attributes: affirm justice, goodness, and beneficence and deny creaturely likeness; leave those who attribute evil acts or likeness to Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد : ولله الأوصاف الحسنى ، وهي الوصف بالعدل والخير والإحسان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r4.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r4.claim: Another view identifies deviation in the names with calling idols gods and deriving al-Lāt from Allah and al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p169#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : إلحادهم في أسمائه : تسميتهم الأصنام آلهة ، واشتقاقهم اللات من الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says all God's names are beautiful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كل أسمائه حسنى

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r2.claim: One meaning of the beautiful names is the names hearts prefer to invoke, such as mercy and forgiveness rather than anger and punishment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r2.anchor: ما مالت إليه القلوب من ذكره بالعفو والرحمة دون السخط والنقمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r3.claim: Alternatively, they are the names God deserves for Himself and His acts, including His being first, everlasting, powerful, knowing, living, one, hearing, seeing, and self-sufficient.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r3.anchor: أسماؤه التي يستحقها لنفسه ولفعله ومنها صفات هي طريقة المعرفة به , وهي تسعة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r4.claim: Calling God by the names may mean invoking Him in petition.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r4.anchor: نداؤه بها عند الرغبة إليه في الدعاء والطلب

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, it may mean glorifying Him by worshipfully remembering these names.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets those who deviate regarding God's names as those who lie.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r7.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r7.claim: Qatada interprets it as associating partners with God.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r8.speaker: الأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses it as distorting or altering the names.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r9.claim: One explanation is that idol names were derived from God's names, such as al-Lat from Allah and al-Uzza from al-Aziz.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r9.anchor: اشتقاقهم آلهتهم من أسماء الله , كما سموا بعضها باللات اشتقاقا من الله , وبعضها بالعزى اشتقاقا من العزيز , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r10.claim: Another explanation is that they named idols gods and called God the father of the Messiah and Ezra.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p281#3/r10.anchor: تسميتهم الأوثان آلهة والله عز وجل أبا المسيح وعزير

MUQATIL:7:180/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:180/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:180/r1.claim: A man prayed invoking both Allah and al-Rahman, and Abu Jahl objected that Muhammad's followers claimed one Lord but invoked two; the verse about God's beautiful names was revealed.
MUQATIL:7:180/r1.anchor: ودعا الرحمن، فقال رجل من مشركى مكة، وهو أبو جهل: أليس يزعم محمد وأصحابه أنهم يعبدون ربا واحدا

MUQATIL:7:180/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:180/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:180/r2.claim: God's beautiful names include al-Rahman, al-Rahim, al-Malik, al-Quddus, al-Salam, al-Mu'min, al-Muhaymin, al-Aziz, al-Jabbar, and al-Mutakabbir, among others.
MUQATIL:7:180/r2.anchor: يعني الرحمن، الرحيم، الملك، القدوس، السلام، المؤمن، المهيمن، العزيز، الجبار، المتكبر

MUQATIL:7:180/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:180/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:7:180/r3.claim: The Prophet told the man to invoke Allah and al-Rahman, explaining that whichever of these names he invoked belonged to the possessor of the beautiful names.
MUQATIL:7:180/r3.anchor: ادع الله، وادع الرحمن، ورغما لأنف المشركين، فإنك ما دعوت من هذه الأسماء، فله الأسماء الحسنى

MUQATIL:7:180/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:180/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:180/r4.claim: Those who incline from the truth give idols God's names, including al-Lat, al-Uzza, Hubal, Asaf, and Na'ila; God forbade naming idols with His name.
MUQATIL:7:180/r4.anchor: في أسمائه عن الحق، فيسمون الآلهة: اللات، والعزى، وهبل، ونحوها، وأساف، ونائلة، فمنعهم الله أن يسموا شيئا من آلهتهم باسم الله

MUQATIL:7:180/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:180/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:180/r5.claim: God will repay those who distort His names with punishment in the Hereafter for what they did.
MUQATIL:7:180/r5.anchor: { سيجزون } بالعذاب في الآخرة { ما كانوا يعملون }

NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r1.claim: God’s names are most beautiful because they indicate beautiful meanings: some belong to His reality, some are valued for their effects, and some invite emulation.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r1.anchor: التى هى أحسن الأسماء لانها تدل على معان حسنة فمنها ما يستحقه بحقائقه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r2.claim: The names grounded in divine reality include the Eternal, Everlasting, All-Powerful, All-Knowing, and the One unlike anything.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r2.anchor: كالقديم قيل كل شيء والباقى بعد كل شيء والقادر على كل شيء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r3.claim: Names appreciated for their effects include Forgiving, Merciful, Appreciative, and Forbearing; other names call for adopting qualities such as generosity.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r3.anchor: ومنها ما تستحسنه الانفس لآثارها كالغفور والرحيم والشكور والحليم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r4.claim: Call God by these names and leave those who depart from their truth by assigning Him unscripted names or descriptions such as body, substance, intellect, or cause.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r4.anchor: واتركوا تسمية الذين يميلون عن الحق والصواب فيها فيسمونه بغير الأسماء الحسنى

NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r5.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v2p48/r5.claim: Hamzah reads the verb for deviating from God’s names with the form yalḥadūn, from laḥada, to turn aside.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r1.claim: The command enjoins exclusive worship and avoidance of polytheists and those who deviate.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r1.anchor: أمر بإخلاص العبادة لله، ومجانبة المشركين والملحدين.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r2.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r2.claim: Maqatil and other commentators report that the verse was revealed after a Muslim prayed using Rahman and Rahim, and a Meccan polytheist mocked the apparent invocation of two lords.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل وغيره من المفسرين: نزلت الآية في رجل من المسلمين

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r3.claim: Reports in al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmit from Abu Hurayra that God has ninety-nine names, with wording differences between the books.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r3.anchor: جاء في كتاب الترمذي وسنن ابن ماجه وغيرهما حديث عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the detailed al-Tirmidhi report is not mass-transmitted; Abu Isa calls it strange and says it is known only through trustworthy Safwan ibn Salih.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية وذكر حديث الترمذي وذلك الحديث ليس بالمتواتر،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi distinguishes the mass-transmitted core: God has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one, and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r5.anchor: وإنما المتواتر منه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r6.claim: Enumerating the names means counting and memorizing them; al-Qurtubi discusses other proposed meanings elsewhere.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r7.claim: He says he discussed the report’s authentication and documented over two hundred names, including disputed ones, and thirty-two introductory chapters on their rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r7.anchor: وذكرنا هناك تصحيح حديث الترمذي، وذكرنا من الأسماء ما اجتمع عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r8.claim: The debate over whether a name is the named entity or the act of naming was discussed in al-Asna.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r8.anchor: واختلف العلماء من هذا الباب في الاسم والمسمى،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r9.speaker: ابن الحصار
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r9.claim: Ibn al-Hassar says the verse applies name both to God as the named one and to naming: God refers to the named, names to designations, and the pronouns return respectively to God and names.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r9.anchor: قال ابن الحصار: وفي هذه الآية وقوع الاسم على المسمى

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r10.claim: Al-Qurtubi invokes the Prophet’s five-names report as an example supporting the distinction between God and His designations.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180/r10.anchor: ومثل ذلك قول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r1.claim: The Prophet’s statement that he has five names, including Muhammad and Ahmad, supports the preceding linguistic point.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r1.anchor: لي خمسة أسماء أنا محمد وأحمد

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r2.speaker: أهل الحق
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r2.claim: The people of truth hold that a name is the named entity or an attribute related to it, distinct from the act of naming.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r2.anchor: والذي يذهب إليه أهل الحق أن الاسم هو المسمى،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi’s first position is that name and named are one, since otherwise God’s names would belong to something other than God.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن العربي عند كلامه على قوله تعالى { ولله الأسماء الحسنى }:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r4.speaker: آخرون
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r4.claim: A second position takes names to mean designations, since God is one while names is plural.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r4.anchor: الثاني قال آخرون: المراد به التسميات

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya says interpreters agree that names here means designations; al-Baqillani explains the ninety-nine as designations for God’s diverse qualities, including attributes of essence and action.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r5.anchor: قلت ذكر ابن عطية في تفسيره أن الأسماء في الآية بمعنى التسميات إجماعا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r6.claim: Abu Bakr explains the designations as expressions for God’s varied qualities, some referring to His essence and others to attributes connected to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r6.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر في كتاب التمهيد: وتأويل قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r7.speaker: آخرون
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r7.claim: A third position says the names mean attributes.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r7.anchor: الثالث قال آخرون منهم: ولله الصفات.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r8.claim: God calls His names beautiful because they point to His oneness, generosity, mercy, and beneficence and sound beautiful to hearts and ears.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r8.anchor: سمى الله سبحانه أسماءه بالحسنى لأنها حسنة في الأسماع والقلوب

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r9.claim: Al-Husna may be a verbal noun used as an adjective, or an elided feminine superlative meaning best.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r9.anchor: والحسنى مصدر وصف به. ويجوز أن يقدر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r10.claim: If it is an adjective for a non-rational plural, it stays singular, as in the cited phrases about other benefits and mountains singing with David.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r10.anchor: وعلى الأول أفرد كما أفرد وصف ما لا يعقل كما قال تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r11.claim: Call on God with the name that suits the request: ask the Merciful for mercy, the Wise for judgment, the Provider for provision, the Guide for guidance, and the Opener to open.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r11.anchor: أي اطلبوا منه بأسمائه فيطلب بكل اسم ما يليق به، تقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r12.claim: A general name can accompany a fitting request, while the all-encompassing name Allah includes every name.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r12.anchor: وإن دعوت بالأعم الأعظم فقلت: يا الله فهو متضمن لكل اسم.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r13.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r13.claim: Ibn al-Arabi cautions against pairing a name with an unsuitable request unless the intended sense fits, and says ordering supplication this way leads to sincerity.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r13.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهكذا، رتب دعاءك تكن من المخلصين.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r14.claim: Al-Qurtubi notes that supplication conditions were treated in al-Baqara and earlier in this sura.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r14.anchor: وقد تقدم في «البقرة» شرائط الدعاء، وفي هذه السورة أيضا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r15.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r15.claim: Ibn al-Arabi includes names such as Completer of His light, Best of heirs, Best of plotters, Fourth of three, Sixth of five, the Good, and Teacher.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r15.anchor: أدخل القاضي أبو بكر ابن العربي عدة من الأسماء في أسمائه سبحانه،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r16.speaker: ابن الحصار
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r16.claim: Ibn al-Hassar says Ibn al-Barjan included names such as the Clean, which had not appeared in scripture or Sunna.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r16.anchor: قال ابن الحصار: واقتدى في ذلك بابن برجان،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r17.claim: Al-Qurtubi rejects the claim that neither the Good nor the Clean occurs in transmitted sources: the Good is in Sahih Muslim and the Clean in al-Tirmidhi.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r17.anchor: قلت: أما ما ذكر من قوله

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r18.claim: Al-Qurtubi introduces a report from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet used a supplication for help, victory, and favorable plotting.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#2/r18.anchor: وخرج عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول في دعائه:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r1.claim: The quoted prayer asks God for help, victory, and a favorable plot; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r1.anchor: رب أعني ولا تعن علي وانصرني ولا تنصر علي

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r2.claim: On that basis, it is permissible to invoke God as Best of plotters and ask Him to plot for the supplicant, not against him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r2.anchor: فعلى هذا جائز أن يقال: يا خير الماكرين امكر لي ولا تمكر علي.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi distinguishes names that may be invoked, those that may name God but not be used in invocation, and those that may do neither, following al-Ashari.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r3.anchor: وما يجوز أن يسمى به ويدعى، وما يجوز أن يسمى به ولا يدعى، وما لا يجوز

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r4.claim: Ilhad means deviation or abandoning the proper course; the root also describes a grave recess because it lies to one side.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r4.anchor: الإلحاد: الميل وترك القصد يقال: ألحد الرجل في الدين.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r5.claim: The verb is read in two forms, both treated as Arabic variants.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r5.anchor: وقرىء «يلحدون» لغتان والإلحاد يكون بثلاثة أوجه:

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r6.claim: The first kind of deviation alters God’s names, as polytheists derived names of their idols from them.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r6.anchor: أحدها بالتغيير فيها كما فعله المشركون،

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada identify the derivations of al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat from divine names as examples of this alteration.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r7.anchor: مناة من المنان قاله ابن عباس وقتادة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r8.claim: A second kind of deviation is adding names to those God has given.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r9.claim: A third kind is subtracting names, as ignorant people do when inventing invocations with names or acts unfitting for God.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r9.anchor: الثالث بالنقصان منها كما يفعله الجهال

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r10.claim: Ibn al-Arabi urges invoking only from the Quran and five canonical hadith books, which include the Muwatta, and warns against inventing personal prayers.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r10.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «فحذار منها، ولا يدعون أحدكم إلا بما في كتاب الله

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r11.claim: Adding names amounts to anthropomorphism and subtracting them to negation; the sound path avoids both.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r11.anchor: الثانية معنى الزيادة في الأسماء التشبيه، والنقصان التعطيل.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r12.speaker: أهل الحق
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r12.claim: The people of truth say religion follows a middle way, without anthropomorphism or negation of attributes.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r12.anchor: ولذلك قال أهل الحق: إن ديننا طريق بين طريقين، لا بتشبيه ولا بتعطيل.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r13.speaker: أبو الحسن البوشنجي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r13.claim: Al-Bushanji defines monotheism as affirming an essence unlike other essences and not stripping it of attributes.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r13.anchor: وسئل الشيخ أبو الحسن البوشنجي عن التوحيد فقال: إثبات ذات

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r14.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets leaving those who deviate as leaving them without debate or confrontation and considers the instruction abrogated by fighting.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#3/r14.anchor: فالآية على هذا منسوخة بالقتال قاله ابن زيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#4/r1.claim: Another interpretation makes leaving those who deviate a threat, as in the commands to leave the isolated man and to let people eat and enjoy themselves; al-Qurtubi says this is apparent because they will be recompensed.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:180#4/r1.anchor: وهو الظاهر من الآية لقوله تعالى: { سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون }.

RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r1.claim: The preceding description of Hell-bound heedlessness is answered by remembrance: heedlessness brings Hell, while remembrance releases one from its punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r1.anchor: وهذا كالتنبيه على أن الموجب لدخول جهنم هو الغفلة عن ذكر الله . والمخلص عن عذاب جهنم هو ذكر الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r2.claim: When the heart forgets God for worldly desires, it enters greed and deprivation and passes from one desire and darkness to another.
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r2.anchor: فإن القلب إذا غفل عن ذكر الله ، وأقبل على الدنيا وشهواتها وقع في باب الحرص وزمهرير الحرمان ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r3.claim: Opening the heart to remembrance and knowledge of God frees it from afflictions and regrets and brings awareness of the Lord of earth and heavens.
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r3.anchor: فإذا انفتح على قلبه باب ذكر الله ومعرفة الله تخلص عن نيران الآفات وعن حسرات الخسارات ، واستشعر بمعرفة رب الأرض والسموات

RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r4.claim: The beautiful names occur in four surahs: this one, al-Isra, Ta-Ha, and al-Hashr.
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r4.anchor: وثانيها : في آخر سورة بني إسرائيل في قوله : { قل ادعوا الله أو ادعوا الرحمان * أياما * تدعوا فله الاسماء الحسنى } ( الإسراء : 11 )

RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r5.claim: Names are words that signify meanings and are beautiful because of the beauty of those meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r5.anchor: { الاسماء } ألفاظ دالة على المعاني فهي إنما تحسن بحسن معانيها ومفهوماتها ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r6.claim: Divine beauty means attributes of perfection and majesty: God needs nothing, while everything else depends on Him.
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r6.anchor: وهي محصورة في نوعين : عدم افتقاره إلى غيره ، وثبوت افتقار غيره إليه .

RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r7.claim: Razi directs readers seeking a full treatment of the divine names and attributes to his book Lawamiʿ al-bayyinat.
RAZI-FULL:v15p54#2/r7.anchor: سميناه ( بلوامع البينات في تفسير الأسماء والصفات )

RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r1.claim: Names may denote the essence, a part of the essence, or an attribute inhering in the essence; the divine essence-name is the Greatest Name.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r1.anchor: الاسم إما أن يكون اسما للذات ، أو لجزء من أجزاء الذات ، أو لصفة خارجة عن الذات قائمة بها . أما اسم الذات فهو المسمى بالاسم الأعظم ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r2.claim: A name for a part of God's essence is impossible: parts entail composition, and anything composite is possible rather than necessary.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r2.anchor: لأن هذا إنما يفعل في الذات المركبة من الأجزاء ، وكل ما كان كذلك فهو ممكن ، فواجب الوجود يمتنع أن يكون له جزء .

RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r3.claim: Attributes are real, relational, privative, or combinations of these kinds.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r3.anchor: الصفة إما أن تكون حقيقية أو إضافية أو سلبية ، أو ما يتركب عن هذه الثلاثة ، وهي أربعة ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r4.claim: Examples of uncombined attributes are existence, on one view, unity, on another, and life; purely relational names include mentioned and known, while holy and peace are privative.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r4.anchor: فكقولنا موجود عند من يقول : الوجود صفة ، أو قولنا واحد ، عند من يقول : الوحدة صفة ثانية ، وكقولنا حي ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r5.claim: Knowledge and power are real attributes related to objects; eternal combines reality with negation, First combines relation with negation, and Wise combines all three kinds.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r5.anchor: فإن العلم صفة حقيقية ، وله تعلق بالمعلوم والقادر ، فإن القدرة صفة حقيقية ، ولها تعلق بالمقدور ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r6.claim: Negations and relations are unlimited, so names tied to God's unlimited acts and possible objects are unlimited too.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r6.anchor: فيحصل بسبب هذين النوعين من الاعتبارات أسماء لا نهاية لها لله تعالى ، لأن مقدوراته غير متناهية ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r7.claim: Since God's essence cannot be grasped and He is known through His acts, greater insight into wisdom in creation yields greater knowledge of His names.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r7.anchor: ولما كان لا سبيل إلى معرفة كنه ذاته ، وإنما السبيل إلى معرفته بمعرفة أفعاله فكل من كان وقوفه على أسرار حكمته في مخلوقاته أكثر ، كان علمه بأسماء الله أكثر .

RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r8.claim: Knowledge of the beautiful names has no end because divine wisdom and its created signs form an endless sea.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55/r8.anchor: ولما كان هذا بحرا لا ساحل له ولا نهاية له ، فكذلك لا نهاية لمعرفة أسماء الله الحسنى .

RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r1.claim: Theologians classify divine attributes as necessary, possible, or impossible, with corresponding names for each class.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r1.anchor: صفات الله تعالى ثلاثة أنواع : ما يجب ، ويجوز ، ويستحيل على الله تعالى . ولله تعالى بحسب كل واحد من هذه الأقسام الثلاثة أسماء مخصوصة .

RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r2.claim: Another classification divides attributes into essential, semantic, and action attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r2.anchor: صفات الله تعالى إما أن تكون ذاتية ، أو معنوية ، أو كانت من صفات الأفعال .

RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r3.claim: Some names, such as generous, merciful, mighty, subtle, great, and creator, can describe people with a different meaning; Allah and al-Rahman are exclusive, and qualifying phrases can make otherwise shared names exclusive.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r3.anchor: فإن هذه الألفاظ يجوز إطلاقها على العباد ، وإن كان معناها في حق الله تعالى مغايرا لمعناها في حق العباد .

RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r4.claim: Allah, al-Rahman, Living, and Wise may be invoked alone; Death-causer and Harmful should be paired with Life-giver and Beneficent.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r4.anchor: ومنها ما لا يكون كذلك ، كقولنا : مميت وضار ، فإنه لا يجوز إفراده بالذكر ، بل يجب أن يقال : يا محيي يا مميت يا ضار يا نافع .

RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r5.claim: Knowledge of God proceeds in order: possible beings require a preponderator, which is known as powerful; perfected acts show knowledge, and power plus knowledge establish life.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r5.anchor: فثبت أن المعلوم منه بعد العلم بكونه مرجحا ، هو كونه / قادرا . ثم إنا بعد هذا نستدل بكون أفعاله محكمة متقنة على كونه عالما ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r6.claim: God's names and attributes are not all known at one level; knowledge of them is a sequence in which later knowledge derives from earlier knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v15p55#2/r6.anchor: بل العلم بها علوم مترتبة يستفاد بعضها من بعض .

RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r1.claim: Only God possesses beautiful names and attributes in themselves: He alone is necessary, while every other being and its qualities depend on Him; creatures possess perfection only by gift.
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r1.anchor: فالله سبحانه كامل لذاته ، وكمال كل ما سواه فهو حاصل بجوده وإحسانه ، فكل كمال وجلال وشرف ، فهو له سبحانه بذاته ولذاته وفي ذاته ، ولغيره على سبيل العارية ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r2.claim: A divine name must convey perfection and majesty; any name that conveys neither cannot properly be applied to God.
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r2.anchor: كل اسم لا يفيد في المسمى صفة كمال وجلال فإنه لا يجوز إطلاقه على الله سبحانه ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r3.speaker: جهم بن صفوان
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r3.claim: Jahm refuses to call God's essence a thing because the word can name the most base and least honorable things, so it conveys no divine distinction.
