RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r3.anchor: نقل عن جهم بن صفوان أنه قال : لا أطلق على ذات الله تعالى اسم الشيء . قال : لأن اسم الشيء يقع على أخس الأشياء وأكثرها حقارة

RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r4.speaker: جهم بن صفوان
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r4.claim: Jahm argues that the verse saying nothing is like God's likeness entails that God is not named a thing, since every thing resembles itself.
RAZI-FULL:v15p56/r4.anchor: { ليس * من شىء } ( الشورى : 11 ) معناه ليس مثل مثله شيء ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r1.speaker: جهم بن صفوان
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r1.claim: Jahm's second argument is that calling God a thing would make Him His own creator, contrary to the statement that He creates everything.
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r1.anchor: { خالق كل شىء } ( الأنعام : 102 الرعد : 16 غافر : 62 ) ولو كان تعالى داخلا تحت اسم الشيء لزم كونه تعالى خالقا لنفسه وهو محال .

RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r2.claim: Against an appeal to exception from a universal, Razi says ordinary usage treats the majority as all and the rare exception as absent; excluding God, the greatest thing, would amount to falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r2.anchor: ثبت بحسب العرف المشهور أنهم يقيمون الأكثر مقام الكل ، ويقيمون الشاذ النادر مقام العدم .

RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r3.speaker: جهم بن صفوان
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r3.claim: Jahm's third argument is that neither revelation nor early devotional practice uses thing as a divine name, so it should be avoided.
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r3.anchor: هذا الاسم ما ورد في كتاب الله ولا سنة رسوله ، وما رأينا أحدا من السلف قال في دعائه ياشيء ، فوجب الامتناع منه ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r4.claim: Razi says the cited question about what is greatest in testimony does not establish that thing is a divine name, as he had explained in al-An'am.
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r4.anchor: { قل أى شىء أكبر شهادة قل الله شهيد بينى وبينكم } ( الأنعام : 19 ) وقد بينا في سورة الأنعام أن هذه الآية لا تدل على المقصود ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r5.claim: Razi distinguishes truth about God's being from permissible invocation: He is truly existent and a reality, but one should not address Him as essence, reality, concept, or known.
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r5.anchor: إن عنيت أنه تعالى في نفسه ذات وحقيقة وثابت وموجود وشيء ، فهو كذلك من غير شك ولا شبهة ، وإن عنيت به أنه هل يجوز أن ينادى بهذه الألفاظ أم لا ؟

RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r6.claim: The early Muslims invoked God by the honored revealed names, not by abstract terms such as essence or concept; therefore such terms should not be used in calling on Him.
RAZI-FULL:v15p57/r6.anchor: وما رأينا ولا سمعنا أن أحدا يقول : يا ذات يا حقيقة يا مفهوم ويا معلوم ، فكان الامتناع عن مثل هذه الألفاظ في معرض النداء والدعاء واجبا لله تعالى .

RAZI-FULL:v15p58/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p58/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p58/r1.claim: The command to invoke God through His beautiful names shows that names are fixed by revelation, not coined by convention; 'Generous' is allowed, but 'liberal,' 'intelligent,' 'physician,' and 'jurist' are not.
RAZI-FULL:v15p58/r1.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن أسماء الله توقيفية لا اصطلاحية . ومما يؤكد هذا أنه يجوز أن يقال : يا جواد ، ولا يجوز أن يقال : يا سخي ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p58/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p58/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p58/r2.claim: Razi argues that names differ from the named entity: the plural indicates multiple names for the one God, and the genitive relation would be impossible if name and named were identical.
RAZI-FULL:v15p58/r2.anchor: لأنها تدل على أن أسماء الله كثيرة لأن لفظ الأسماء لفظ الجمع ، وهي تفيد الثلاثة فما فوقها ، فثبت أن أسماء الله كثيرة ولا شك أن الله واحد ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r1.claim: Calling upon God by His names requires understanding their meanings and reasoned knowledge that He is Lord and Creator with holy attributes.
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r1.anchor: وهذه الدعوة لا تتأتى إلا إذا عرف معاني تلك الأسماء ، وعرف بالدليل أن له إلها وربا خالقا موصوفا بتك الصفات الشريفة المقدسة ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r2.claim: Al-Halimi's al-Minhaj details the conditions of supplication; its best teaching is to hold together the Lord's majesty and the servant's humility.
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r2.anchor: وأحسن ما فيه أن يكون مستحضرا لأمرين : أحدهما : عزة الربوبية . والثانية : ذلة العبودية .

RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r3.claim: Without those inward states, invocation has little benefit; Razi illustrates the point through the opening Allahu akbar of prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r3.anchor: فأما إذا لم يكن كذلك كان قليل الفائدة ، وأنا أذكر لهذا المعنى مثالا ، وهو أن من أراد أن يقول في تحريمة صلاته الله أكبر ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.claim: For that takbir, one should contemplate divine wisdom and power in oneself and in the created orders, from people, animals, plants, and minerals through the heavens, Throne, and angels, as far as understanding reaches.
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.anchor: ثم يستحضر آثار قدرة الله تعالى في تخليق طبقات العناصر السفلية والعلوية ، ثم يستحضر آثار قدرة الله تعالى في تخليق أطباق السموات على سعتها وعظمها ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r5.claim: In Allahu akbar, Allah names the creator who brought and ordered all things; akbar declares Him beyond likeness and beyond even comparison as greater than them.
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r5.anchor: ويقول الله أكبر ، ويشير بقوله الله إلى الموجود الذي خلق هذه الأشياء وأخرجها من العدم إلى الوجود / ورتبها بما لها من الصفات والنعوت ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r6.claim: This example lets the reader gauge remembrance joined with knowledge and awareness, which opens insight into the verse's hidden meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v15p58#2/r6.anchor: فقس الذكر الحاصل مع العرفان والشعور ، وعند هذا ينفتح على عقلك نسمة من الأسرار المودعة تحت قوله : { والله * الاسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها } .

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r1.speaker: حمزة
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r1.claim: Hamza reads yalḥidūn; Asim and al-Kisa'i agree with this form in al-Nahl.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة { يلحدون } ووافقه عاصم والكسائي في النحل .

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r2.claim: Al-Farra' treats yalḥidūn and yalḥadūn as dialectal forms, corresponding to the verbs laḥada and alḥada.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r2.anchor: قال الفراء : { يلحدون } و { يلحدون } لغتان : يقال : لحدت لحدا وألحدت ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit defines a heretic as one who departs from truth and introduces into it what does not belong there.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r3.anchor: قال ابن السكيت : الملحد العادل عن الحق المدخل فيه ما ليس منه .

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r4.claim: Abu Amr defines ilhad as turning away from uprightness; the grave's lateral niche is called laḥd for the same directional reason.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو من أهل اللغة : الإلحاد : العدل عن الاستقامة والانحراف عنها . ومنه اللحد الذي يحفر في جانب القبر .

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r5.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi prefers the common reading because ilhad is the more common form, as shown by the Hajj verse and the usual word mulḥid.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r5.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : والأجود قراءة العامة لقوله تعالى : { ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد } ( الحج : 25 ) والإلحاد أكثر في كلامهم

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r6.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r6.claim: The scholars identify three forms of ilhad in God's names; the first applies divine names to others, as idolaters called their idols gods.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r6.anchor: قال المحققون : الإلحاد في أسماء الله يقع على ثلاثة أوجه : الأول : إطلاق أسماء الله المقدسة الطاهرة على غير الله ، مثل أن الكفار كانوا يسمون الأوثان بآلهة ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r7.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r7.claim: They explain the idol names al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat as derived respectively from al-Ilah, al-Aziz, and al-Mannan.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك أنهم سموا أصناما لهم باللات والعزى والمناة ، واشتقاق اللات من الإله ، والعزى من العزيز ، واشتقاق مناة من المنان .

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r8.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r8.claim: They also cite Musaylima the Liar's appropriation of the divine name al-Rahman.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r8.anchor: وكان مسيلمة الكذاب لقب نفسه بالرحمن .

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r9.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r9.claim: The second form gives God an impermissible name, such as calling Him the father of Christ or using the Christian formula Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r9.anchor: أن يسموا الله بما لا يجوز تسميته به ، مثل تسمية من سماه أبا للمسيح . وقول جمهور النصارى : أب ، وابن ، وروح القدس ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r10.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r10.claim: Other examples of the second form are the Karramiyya calling God a body and Mu'tazilites saying that a divine action would make Him foolish and blameworthy, which the source calls discourteous language.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r10.anchor: ومثل أن الكرامية يطلقون لفظ الجسم على الله سبحانه ويسمونه به ، ومثل أن المعتزلة قد يقولون في أثناء كلامهم ، لو فعل تعالى كذا وكذا لكان سفيها مستحقا للذم ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r11.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r11.claim: Razi's school says semantic truth alone does not license a divine name: despite creating every body, one should not invoke God as creator of worms, apes, or ticks, but with noble sanctifying names.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r11.anchor: وليس كل ما صح معناه جاز إطلاقه باللفظ في حق الله ، فإنه ثبت بالدليل أنه سبحانه هو الخالق لجميع الأجسام ، ثم لا يجوز أن يقال : يا خالق الديدان والقرود والقردان ،

RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r12.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r12.claim: The third form is invoking God with a word whose meaning and referent the speaker does not know, since it might refer to something unworthy of divine majesty.
RAZI-FULL:v15p59/r12.anchor: والثالث : أن يذكر العبد ربه بلفظ لا يعرف معناه ولا يتصور مسماه ، فإنه ربما كان مسماه أمرا غير لائق بجلال / الله ،

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r1.claim: Following the heedless of verse 179, the verse tells people to call upon God by His Most Beautiful Names; commentators connect the verb with supplication and remembrance of God.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r1.anchor: The verb that translates call upon also means “to supplicate” and is here connected by commentators with the practice of remembering and invoking God

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r2.claim: The verse is a scriptural basis for dhikr in Islamic spirituality, especially Sufism.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r2.anchor: This verse is thus one of the scriptural bases for the practice of dhikr in Islamic spirituality and especially Sufism

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r3.claim: God's Most Beautiful Names also appear in 20:8 and 59:24, while 17:110 similarly commands invocation by them.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r3.anchor: Mention of God’s Most Beautiful Names is also found in 20:8; 59:24; and a similar command to call upon them is made in 17:110

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r4.claim: The term al-ḥusnā relates to goodness and virtue, and the Names are beautiful both to the ear and to the heart.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r4.anchor: a word also related to goodness and virtue, and are said to be beautiful to the ear as well as the heart (Q)

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r5.claim: A widely reported hadith underlies the traditional teaching that God has ninety-nine Beautiful Names.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r5.anchor: God is traditionally said to have ninety-nine Beautiful Names

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r6.claim: Lists of the Names vary and may exceed ninety-nine; they are grounded in Quranic descriptions, and some derive from divine actions described there.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r6.anchor: While the list of those Names varies slightly in different reports, and several lists contain more than ninety-nine

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r7.claim: The Names do not compromise God's Oneness or divide Him into parts; they express qualities of His undifferentiated Essence that become differentiated through self-manifestation and perceived by the caller.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r7.anchor: the Names are considered to represent Attributes or Qualities of His undifferentiated Essence, which are differentiated through the Self-manifestation of the Essence

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r8.claim: The Names reveal both essential divine attributes and the different ways God relates to creation.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r8.anchor: They also reveal different Attributes of God, some pertaining to His Essence, and others to the different ways in which He relates to His creation

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r9.speaker: al-Ṭabrisī
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r9.claim: Each Name has a real Divine Presence or Quality; there are no empty titles for God.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r9.anchor: as al-Ṭabrisī notes there are no empty titles for God

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r10.claim: Islamic metaphysics regards the cosmos as reflections or theophanies of the Divine Names and Qualities.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r10.anchor: the whole of the cosmos is considered to be in reality nothing but reflections or theophanies

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r11.claim: The Names and Qualities are major concerns in theology, philosophy, and Sufism; the science of Divine Names includes al-jafr, symbolic numerology of Names and their letters.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r11.anchor: the science of Divine Names (ʿilm al-asmāʾ), which includes the science of al-jafr—that is, the science of the symbolic numerical significance

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r12.speaker: most Islamic thinkers
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r12.claim: They identify God's Names as Attributes, usually dividing them into Attributes of Essence and of action, while traditional sources differ on classification and on whether Attributes are distinct from or identical with Essence.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r12.anchor: Most Islamic thinkers agree that God’s Names are His Attributes

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r13.speaker: Islamic esoterism
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r13.claim: It regards God and His Names as one; God is present in the sanctified Names, each a ladder leading to Him.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r13.anchor: In Islamic esoterism, God and His Names are considered one

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r14.claim: Names are also divided into those of Beauty, such as Compassionate and Merciful, and Majesty, such as Judge and Compeller.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r14.anchor: such as Compassionate, Merciful, Gentle, Kind, and Pardoner, and those of Majesty

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r15.claim: Some Names can be manifested in humans while others belong to God alone; human names may use the former but not the latter, and some Names fit both categories.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r15.anchor: the Names have been also divided into those that could be manifested in human beings (Kind, Generous) and those that belong to God alone

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r16.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r16.claim: One view says all God's Names are Most Beautiful; another narrows the phrase to Names of Beauty, encouraging invocation for mercy while discouraging invocation of Names of Majesty or Wrath.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r16.anchor: some suggest that here the Most Beautiful Names refers specifically to the Names of Beauty, which believers are encouraged to call upon

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r17.speaker: other commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r17.claim: Others allow calling God by any Name or description found in the Quran, citing expressions such as completer of His Light and best of plotters.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r17.anchor: Others assert that one can call upon God by any Name or description of God found in the Quran

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r18.claim: God's supreme Name is Allāh, said to encompass all His other Names.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r18.anchor: God’s supreme Name is Allāh, which is said to encompass all of His other Names

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r19.claim: Sufis commonly repeat Allāh or other Names prescribed by a shaykh to cultivate virtues and treat spiritual ailments, figuratively transmuting the soul from lead into gold.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r19.anchor: it is also common for them to repeatedly invoke other Divine Names under the instruction of a shaykh

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r20.speaker: Sufi commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r20.claim: They view Quranic Names and Attributes as limits of human knowledge of God and as gates to His infinite reality, enabling knowledge beyond what is humanly accessible.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r20.anchor: but also gates to His infinite Reality and the forms made available to human beings

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r21.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r21.claim: Those who deviate may use specifically human attributes such as father or son for God, attribute evil actions or intentions to Him, or anthropomorphize Him with ignorant or unworthy descriptions.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r21.anchor: Those who deviate with regard to His Names are said to be those who refer to Him using specifically human attributes, such as “father” or “son”

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r22.speaker: several commentators
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r22.claim: They say God should be named only with descriptions in the Quran or Sunnah, even when another description is synonymous with a scriptural Name.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r22.anchor: Several commentators assert that one should not refer to God using any name or description not found in the Quran or the Sunnah

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r23.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r23.claim: Ritual invocation requires Arabic, but private supplication outside canonical prayer or Sufi dhikr may use non-Arabic names such as Persian Khudā or English God.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r23.anchor: Whenever the invocation of God’s Names is done ritually, the Names have to be invoked in Arabic

STUDYQURAN:7:180/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r24.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r24.claim: Deviation can mean using God's Names or their derivatives for false gods; the pagan Makkans worshipped Allāt, apparently a feminine form of Allāh.
STUDYQURAN:7:180/r24.anchor: To deviate with regard to His Names can also refer to those who use His Names or derivations from them to designate false gods or idols

SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r1.claim: The stronger analysis makes الحسنى the feminine of أحسن; nonrational broken plurals may take feminine adjectives, while masculine matching is also possible.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r1.anchor: والجمع المكسر لغير العاقل يجوز أن يوصف بما يوصف

SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r2.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r2.claim: A poetic example supports the alternative that الحسنى is a verbal noun on the fuʿlā pattern, like الرجعى and البقيا.

SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r3.claim: الأسماء here means the words that designate God, such as Allah and al-Raḥmān.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r3.anchor: الألفاظ الدالة على الباري تعالى كالله والرحمن

SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the intended meaning is the names' designations by consensus; the author objects that a verbal noun is not what one invokes.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r4.anchor: المراد بها التسميات إجماعا من المتأولين لا يمكن غيره

SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r5.claim: On the author's preferred explanation of دعوه, it means call upon God by these names, as in calling Him Allah or al-Raḥmān.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r5.anchor: نادوه بها، كقولهم: يا الله يا رحمان

SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r6.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:7:180/r6.claim: A further interpretation takes فادعوه as name Him with these names, like naming a son Zayd.

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads يلحدون with open yāʾ and ḥāʾ from the triliteral لحد; the other readers use ʾalḥada with a damma and kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r1.anchor: يلحدون بفتح الياء والحاء من لحد ثلاثيا

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r2.speaker: ابن السكيت
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt treats the two readings as synonymous, both meaning to incline or deviate, and glosses them as turning away from truth.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r2.anchor: وإلى كونهما بمعنى واحد ذهب ابن السكيت

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r3.claim: The noun لحد is connected with the grave niche because it is dug to one side, unlike a central الضريح.

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r4.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r4.claim: A poet's use of الملحد illustrates that أَلحد is more common in usage than لحد.

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r5.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r5.claim: Al-Kisāʾī distinguishes the roots: لحد means to lean or take refuge, while ألحد means to incline or deviate; he also reports ألحد as turn away and لحد as lean.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r5.anchor: وقال غيره: " لحد بمعنى ركن وانضوى، وألحد: مال وانحرف " قاله الكسائي

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda transmits from al-Aṣmaʿī that ألحد means dispute or argue, whereas لحد means turn aside or lean.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r6.anchor: وروى أبو عبيدة عن الأصمعي: " ألحد: مارى وجادل

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r7.claim: The common reading with ألحد is favored by agreement with the Qurʾanic wording بإلحاد.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r7.anchor: ورجحت قراءة العامة بالإجماع على قوله

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r8.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r8.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says Arabs scarcely use the active participle لاحد; the author says its rarity is shown by this absence but notes the attested phrase لحده اللاحد.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r8.anchor: وقال الواحدي: " ولا يكاد يسمع من العرب لاحد

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r9.claim: Ilḥād may mean deriving idols' names from God's names, such as al-Lāt from Allah, al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz, and Manāt from al-Mannān.

SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, ilḥād may mean attributing to God names that do not befit His majesty.
SAMIN-DURR:7:180#2/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد سموه بما لا يليق بجلاله

TAB-FULL:v10p596/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p596/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's beautiful names include al-Aziz and al-Jabbar, and all God's names are beautiful.
TAB-FULL:v10p596/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها} [الأعراف: 180] ومن أسمائه: العزيز الجبار، وكل أسماء الله حسن

TAB-FULL:v10p596/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v10p596/r2.claim: The Prophet says God has ninety-nine names, and whoever enumerates them all will enter Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v10p596/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: «إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما، مائة إلا واحدا، من أحصاها كلها دخل الجنة»

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r1.claim: Al-Tabari identifies those who deviate concerning God's names as polytheists who redirect divine names to idols, deriving al-Lat from Allah and al-Uzza from al-Aziz.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r1.anchor: اشتقاقا لها من اسم الله الذي هو العزيز

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the idolaters' deviation as naming al-Lat among God's names.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} [الأعراف: 180] قال: إلحاد الملحدين أن دعوا اللات في أسماء الله

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says al-Uzza was derived from al-Aziz and al-Lat from Allah.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} [الأعراف: 180] قال: اشتقوا العزى من العزيز، واشتقوا اللات من الله

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas gives another gloss of ilhad: denial or falsehood.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} [الأعراف: 180] قال: الإلحاد: التكذيب

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r5.claim: Qatada glosses ilhad as associating partners with God.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r5.anchor:
عن معمر، عن قتادة
: " {يلحدون} [الأعراف: 180] قال: يشركون

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r6.claim: The root of ilhad means turning away from the intended course, injustice, or avoidance, then comes to denote anything crooked; a grave's lahd is its side recess, not the center.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r6.anchor: وأصل الإلحاد في كلام العرب: العدول عن القصد، والجور عنه، والإعراض، ثم يستعمل في كل معوج غير مستقيم

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r7.speaker: الكسائي
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r7.claim: Al-Kisa'i distinguishes ilhad as deviation from the course from lahd as leaning toward something, and reads the Nahl occurrence with fatḥa as meaning leaning.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r7.anchor: وقد ذكر عن الكسائي أنه كان يفرق بين الإلحاد واللحد، فيقول في الإلحاد: إنه العدول عن القصد

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r8.claim: Other Arabists treat ilhad and lahd as two dialect forms with the same meaning in this passage.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r8.anchor: وأما سائر أل المعرفة بكلام العرب فيرون أن معناهما واحد، وأنهما لغتان جاءتا في حرف واحد بمعنى واحد

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r9.speaker: عامة قراء أهل المدينة وبعض البصريين والكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r9.claim: Most Medinan readers and some Basran and Kufan readers pronounce yalhidun with a damma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ, from alhada, throughout the Qur'an.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r9.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء أهل المدينة وبعض البصريين والكوفيين: {يلحدون} [الأعراف: 180] بضم الياء وكسر الحاء من ألحد يلحد في جميع القرآن

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r10.speaker: عامة قراء أهل الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r10.claim: Most Kufan readers pronounce yalhadun with fatḥa on both yāʾ and ḥāʾ, deriving it from lahada.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء أهل الكوفة: (يلحدون) بفتح الياء والحاء من لحد يلحد

TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r11.claim: Al-Tabari says both readings are valid dialects with the same meaning, so either is correct; he prefers the reading with damma on yāʾ.
TAB-FULL:v10p596#2/r11.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك أنهما لغتان بمعنى واحد فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب الصواب في ذلك. غير أني أختار القراءة بضم الياء

TAB-FULL:v10p599/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the form ألحد is the more familiar and eloquent of the two language variants.

TAB-FULL:v10p599/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the command to leave those who distort God's names was abrogated by fighting.
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r2.anchor: وكان ابن زيد يقول في قوله: {وذروا الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} [الأعراف: 180] : إنه منسوخ

TAB-FULL:v10p599/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects abrogation: this is not an order to let the polytheists speak until permission to fight, but a threat and warning.
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r3.anchor: ليس بأمر من الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بترك المشركين أن يقولوا ذلك حتى يأذن له في قتالهم، وإنما هو تهديد من الله

TAB-FULL:v10p599/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r4.claim: The imperative expresses a threat: God gives the name-distorters respite until their appointed term, then repays their disbelief, distortion, and rejection of the Messenger; compare 15:3 and 29:66.
TAB-FULL:v10p599/r4.anchor: فسوف يجزون إذا جاءهم أجل الله الذي أجله إليهم جزاء أعمالهم التي كانوا يعملونها قبل ذلك من الكفر بالله والإلحاد في أسمائه

TABATABAI:7:180-186/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r1.claim: These verses continue the preceding argument by restating that guidance and misguidance turn on calling God by His beautiful names or distorting them.
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r1.anchor: بيان الآيات متصلة بما قبلها، وهي بمنزلة تجديد البيان لما انتهى إليه الكلام في الآيات السابقة

TABATABAI:7:180-186/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r2.claim: By natural disposition, people agree that the visible world depends on God, who orders it, originates and receives all things, and gives it its beauty and perfection.
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r2.anchor: حقيقة هي المقومة لاعيان أجزائها الناظمة نظامها، وهو الله سبحانه الذي منه يبتدء كل شيء وإليه يعود كل شيء

TABATABAI:7:180-186/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r3.claim: One group names God only with attributes of perfection or names that negate every defect, thereby calling on Him by the beautiful names.
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r3.anchor: صنف يسمونه بما لا يشتمل من المعنى إلا على ما يليق أن ينسب إلى ساحته من الصفات المبينة للكمال

TABATABAI:7:180-186/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r4.claim: A second group distorts divine names by assigning creation, life, or provision to matter or time, good to idols, divine prerogatives to prophets or saints, or independent power to created causes.
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r4.anchor: الماديين والدهريين الذين ينسبون الخلق والإحياء والرزق وغير ذلك إلى المادة أو الدهر، وكالوثنيين الناسبين الخير والنفع إلى آلهتهم

TABATABAI:7:180-186/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r5.claim: A third group believes in God but attributes defects to Him, including body, location, sensory apprehension, humanlike knowledge, will, or power, temporal persistence, injustice, and ignorance.
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r5.anchor: يثبتون له من صفات النقص والأفعال الدينية ما هو منزه عنه كالاعتقاد بأن له جسما، وأن له مكانا، وأن الحواس المادية يمكن أن تتعلق به

TABATABAI:7:180-186/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r6.claim: The three groups reduce to two: those who worship God by His beautiful names are rightly guided, while those who misname Him or assign His name elsewhere are astray and headed for the Fire according to their error.
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r6.anchor: وترجع الأصناف الثلاثة في الحقيقة إلى صنفين صنف يدعونه بالأسماء الحسنى ويعبدون الله ذو الجلال والإكرام

TABATABAI:7:180-186/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r7.claim: Guidance originates wholly with God; misguidance itself is a privation, but God makes it persistent by withholding success as recompense, through gradual enticement and respite.
TABATABAI:7:180-186/r7.anchor: فإنها صفة جميلة وله تعالى حقيقتها، وأما الضلال فلا ينسب إليه سبحانه أصله لأنه بحسب الحقيقة عدم اهتداء المحل بهداية الله

TABATABAI:7:180/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180/r1.claim: A name linguistically denotes an object, either with descriptive meaning or as a bare reference to the essence; the phrase beautiful names points to descriptive names, not bare proper names.
TABATABAI:7:180/r1.anchor: الاسم بحسب اللغة ما يدل به على الشيء سواء أفاد مع ذلك معنى وصفيا كاللفظ الذي يشار به إلى الشيء

TABATABAI:7:180/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180/r2.claim: Not every descriptive meaning is a beautiful name: a name must express the best perfection when considered with the divine essence, without inseparable deficiency.
TABATABAI:7:180/r2.anchor: ولا كل معنى وصفي حسن بل ما كا أحسن بالنسبة إلى غيره إذا اعتبرا مع الذات المتعالية

TABATABAI:7:180/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180/r3.claim: Courage and chastity are unsuitable divine names because they imply bodily particularity, whereas generosity, justice, and mercy can be purified of such limitation.
TABATABAI:7:180/r3.anchor: فالشجاع والعفيف من الأسماء الحسنة لكنهما لا يليقان بساحة قدسه لإنبائهما عن خصوصية جسمانية

TABATABAI:7:180/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180/r4.claim: Human terms such as knowledge, life, and power acquire bodily limitations in their created instances, but when abstracted to their perfect meanings they may be attributed to God without those limitations.
TABATABAI:7:180/r4.anchor: غير أنا إذا جردنا معانيها عن خصوصيات المادة عاد العلم وهو الإحاطة بالشيء بحضوره عنده، والقدرة هي المنشئية للشيء بإيجاده

TABATABAI:7:180#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r1.claim: Putting the predicate first and making names definite and plural indicates restriction and generality: every best name belongs to God alone in its true reality, while creatures possess only what He grants.
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r1.anchor: وهو يفيد الحصر، وجيء بالأسماء محلى باللام، والجمع المحلى باللام يفيد العموم

TABATABAI:7:180#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r2.claim: Verses on power, might, knowledge, and life support God's exclusive ownership of the reality of every beautiful name, which He grants to others as He wills.
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r2.anchor: وظاهر الآيات بل نص بعضها يؤيد هذا المعنى كقوله أن القوة لله جميعا

TABATABAI:7:180#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r3.claim: The proposed definite reference in al-asmāʾ has no textual or contextual support; its only basis is familiarity with reports enumerating the beautiful names, which will be discussed later.
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r3.anchor: للعهد مما لا دليل عليه ولا في القرائن الحافة بالآيات ما يؤيده

TABATABAI:7:180#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r4.claim: Commentators allow fā-duʿūhu bihā to mean name Him, call upon Him, or worship Him as possessing the perfections indicated by these names.
TABATABAI:7:180#2/r4.anchor: إما من الدعوة بمعنى التسمية كقولنا دعوته زيدا ودعوتك أبا عبد الله

TABATABAI:7:180-181/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r1.claim: Qur'anic usage supports understanding invocation as worship: 17:110, 40:60, 46:5–6, and 40:65 connect calling on God with worship and sincere religion.
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r1.anchor: حيث ذكر أولا الدعاء ثم بدله ثانيا من العبادة إيماء إلى اتحادهما

TABATABAI:7:180-181/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r2.claim: The intended meaning is to worship God through all His beautiful names; naming and calling Him by them are attendant parts of worship. The warning about those who distort names supports this reading.
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r2.anchor: فمعنى الآية - والله أعلم - ولله جميع الأسماء التي هي أحسن فاعبدوه وتوجهوا إليه بها

TABATABAI:7:180-181/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r3.claim: Laḥd and ilḥād both mean departing from the middle toward a side; the grave niche is called laḥd because it lies at the side, unlike a central burial niche.
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r3.anchor: اللحد والإلحاد بمعنى واحد وهو التطرف والميل عن الوسط إلى أحد الجانبين، ومنه لحد القبر لكونه في جانبه

TABATABAI:7:180-181/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r4.claim: One reading has yalḥadūn with fatḥa on the yāʾ from the basic form and another has yulḥidūn with ḍamma in the causative form; both carry the same meaning. Some lexicographers distinguish ilḥād as disputation.
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r4.anchor: فقرائه يلحدون بفتح الياء من المجرد، ويلحدون بضم الياء من باب الإفعال بمعنى واحد، ونقل عن بعض اللغويين

TABATABAI:7:180-181/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r5.claim: The fa separating the warning from the promise marks the latter as an answer to an implied question about what will become of the name distorters.
TABATABAI:7:180-181/r5.anchor: الآية بالفصل لأنه بمنزلة الجواب لسؤال مقدر كأنه لما قيل

TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r1.claim: God owns every perfection found in existence, so He is living, powerful, knowing, hearing, seeing, provider, merciful, mighty, creator, life-giver, death-giver, originator, restorer, and raiser.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r1.anchor: فهو سبحانه يملك ما وجدناه في الوجود من صفة كمال كالحياة والقدرة والعلم والسمع والبصر والرزق والرحمة

TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r2.claim: Names such as al-Subbūḥ and al-Quddūs negate every privative quality and defect; this natural reasoning for affirming divine names is confirmed by scripture.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r2.anchor: وهو السبوح القدوس العلي الكبير المتعال إلى غير ذلك نعني بها نفي كل نعت عدمي وكل صفة نقص عنه

TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r3.claim: The word al-malik with kasra and al-mulk with ḍamma both express God's absolute ownership and dominion, as many verses affirm.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#2/r3.anchor: وقد صدقنا كتاب الله في ذلك حيث أثبت الملك - بكسر الميم - والملك - بضم الميم - له على الإطلاق

TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r1.claim: God's oneness subdues and encompasses everything, expressing that He is beyond the limits that apply to creatures.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r1.anchor: فله الوحدة التي تقهر كل شيء من قبله فتحيط به

TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r2.claim: God's attributes are identical with His essence and with each other in reality, differing only by concept.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r2.anchor: أن صفاته تعالى عين ذاته، وكل صفة عين الصفة الأخرى، فلا تمايز إلا بحسب المفهوم

TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r3.claim: If an attribute differed from God's essence or from another attribute, each would limit the other and entail boundedness, composition, and dependence.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r3.anchor: لكان كل منها يحد الآخر والآخر ينتهي إليه فكان محدود وحد ومتناه ونهاية فكان تركيب وفقر

TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r4.claim: The divine attributes are identical with God's essence and with one another in reality, differing only in concept; otherwise they would limit each other and entail composition and dependence, contrary to indivisible divine unity.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#3/r4.anchor: وهذه صفة أحديته تعالى لا ينقسم من جهة من الجهات، ولا يتكثر في خارج ولا في ذهن

TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r1.claim: He rejects reducing knowledge, power, life, and all other attributes to mere negations, since that would deny every perfection and conflicts with natural disposition and Qur'anic wording.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r1.anchor: ومما تقدم يظهر فساد قول من قال إن معاني صفاته تعالى ترجع إلى النفى رعاية لتنزيهه عن صفات خلقه

TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r2.claim: He also rejects treating attributes as additions to the essence or denying attributes while affirming only their effects; the argument is deferred for fuller treatment.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r2.anchor: ونظيره القول بكون صفاته زائدة على ذاته أو نفي الصفات وإثبات آثارها وغير ذلك مما قيل في الصفات

TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r3.claim: Attributes divide into positive perfections such as knowledge and life, and negative names such as al-Subbūḥ and al-Quddūs that express transcendence from defect.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r3.anchor: من صفات الله سبحانه ما يفيد معنى ثبوتيا كالعلم والحياة وهي المشتملة على معنى الكمال، ومنها ما يفيد معنى السلب وهي التي للتنزيه

TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r4.claim: Active attributes such as creating and providing presuppose the essence and are derived from God's acts; unlike essential attributes, they are not intrinsic acquisitions.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r4.anchor: ومنها ما يحتاج في تحققه إلى فرض تحقق الذات قبلا كالخلق والرزق وهي الصفات الفعلية، وهي زائدة على الذات منتزعة عن مقام الفعل

TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r5.claim: Attributes also divide into nonrelational self-attributes, self-attributes with an external relation, and purely relational attributes, such as life, creating, and being Creator or provider.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r5.anchor: ولها انقسام آخر إلى النفسية والإضافية فما لا إضافة في معناها إلى الخارج عن مقام الذات كالحياة نفسي

TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r6.claim: A quality denotes a meaning attributed to the essence, while a name denotes the essence under a quality; life and knowledge are attributes, and living and knowing are names.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#4/r6.anchor: لا فرق بين الصفة والاسم غير أن الصفة تدل على معنى من المعاني يتلبس به الذات أعم من العينية والغيرية

TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r1.claim: People infer God's names from perfections observed in the world, because God owns and gives them; observed deficiencies show that He is free of them and possesses their opposite perfections.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r1.anchor: وقد تقدم أنا في سلوكنا الفطري إلى الأسماء إنما تفطنا بها من جهة ما شاهدناه في الكون من صفات الكمال

TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r2.claim: Divine attributes mediate between God and creation: His knowledge, power, provision, and beneficence supply creatures' corresponding needs and deficiencies.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r2.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن جهات الخلقة وخصوصيات الوجود التي في الأشياء ترتبط إلى ذاته المتعالية من طريق صفاته الكريمة

TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r3.claim: People fittingly invoke God by names suited to their needs: the one seeking wealth uses the Rich, Mighty, or Powerful, while the sick person calls on the Healer, Clement, or Merciful.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r3.anchor: فمن يسأل الله الغنى ليس يقول يا مميت يا مذل أغنني، وإنما يدعوه بأسمائه الغني والعزيز والقادر مثلا

TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r4.claim: The Qur'an validates this practice by ending passages with names suited to their meaning and using names to explain its claims; it is the only revealed scripture known to the author that teaches divine names.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r4.anchor: والقرآن الكريم يصدقنا في هذا السلوك والقضاء، وهو أصدق شاهد على صحة هذا النظر فتراه يذيل آياته الكريمة بما يناسب مضامين متونها

TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r5.claim: Creatures relate to God through His names and their widespread effects: manifestations of beauty and majesty connect them to those names, and the names connect them to the sustaining divine essence.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#5/r5.anchor: فآثار الجمال والجلال في هذا العالم هي التي تربطنا بأسماء جماله وجلاله من حياة وعلم وقدرة وعزة وعظمة وكبرياء

TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r1.claim: Divine names vary in scope in correspondence with their effects: knowledge branches into hearing, sight, imagination, and understanding, while broader provision and mercy encompass further qualities.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r1.anchor: موهبة العلم التي عندنا تنشعب منها شعب السمع والبصر والخيال والتعقل

TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r2.claim: Names form a hierarchy from specific names to the all-encompassing greatest name; effects and blessings widen with a name's generality, and all effects ultimately submit to it.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r2.anchor: حتى تنتهي إلى اسم الله الأكبر الذي يسع وحده جميع حقائق الأسماء

TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r3.claim: A popular belief treats the greatest name as an unknown verbal formula that guarantees a response and can subject everything to human will.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r3.anchor: شاع بين الناس أنه اسم لفظي من أسماء الله سبحانه إذا دعي به استجيب

TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r4.speaker: أصحاب العزائم والدعوات
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r4.claim: Practitioners of invocations claim the name has a naturally indicative utterance, with letters varying by need and methods for extracting and composing them.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r4.anchor: وفي مزعمة أصحاب العزائم والدعوات أن له لفظا يدل عليه بطبعه

TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r5.claim: Reports suggest a verbal composition: the basmala is especially close to the greatest name, its letters occur in cited passages, and Asif used its letters to bring the Queen of Sheba's throne instantly.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r5.anchor: وما ورد أن آصف بن برخيا وزير سليمان دعا بما عنده من حروف اسم الله الأعظم

TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r6.claim: Another report says the greatest name has seventy-three letters, of which God gave the prophets seventy-two and reserved one in the unseen.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#6/r6.anchor: أن الاسم الأعظم على ثلاث وسبعين حرفا قسم الله بين أنبيائه اثنين وسبعين منها

TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r1.claim: Real causal influence depends on the strength of existents and affinity between cause and effect; a sound or mental concept cannot overpower existence because it is itself dependent on human will.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r1.anchor: فإن التأثير الحقيقي يدور مدار وجود الأشياء في قوته وضعفه، والمسانخة بين المؤثر والمتأثر

TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r2.claim: Divine names, including the greatest name, mediate effects in the cosmos through their realities; God acts through the fitting attribute, not through a word, mental concept, or independent entity.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r2.anchor: لكنها انما تؤثر بحقائقها لا بالألفاظ الدالة في لغة كذا عليها

TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r3.claim: The promise to answer a caller (2:186) requires a true request directed to God; one who turns from every other cause reaches the reality of the name suited to the need, whose effect follows its scope.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r3.anchor: فمن انقطع عن كل سبب واتصل بربه لحاجة من حوائجه فقد اتصل بحقيقة الاسم المناسب لحاجته

TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r4.claim: The reports and prayers about the greatest name should be understood as connection to the name's reality; teaching a servant a name opens this way of turning to God, while words and meanings only preserve realities.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا يجب أن يحمل ما ورد من الروايات والأدعية في هذا الباب دون الاسم اللفظي أو مفهومه

TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r5.claim: A name may be exclusive to God; al-Ilāh is exclusive as a proper name, whereas al-Raḥmān has a shared meaning as one of the beautiful names.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#7/r5.anchor: أن الاسم الخاص ربما يطلق على ما لا يسمى به غير الله سبحانه كما قيل به في الاسمين الله، والرحمن

TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r1.claim: Allah is a proper name exclusive to God rather than a name in the technical sense under discussion; al-Raḥmān has a shared meaning, and the legal inquiry lies outside this exegetical discussion.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r1.anchor: أما لفظ الجلالة فهو علم له تعالى خاص به ليس اسما بالمعنى الذي نبحث عنه

TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r2.claim: Scripture does not set a fixed number of beautiful names: 20:8, 7:180, and 59:24 indicate that every name whose meaning is most beautiful belongs to God.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r2.anchor: لا دليل في الآيات الكريمة على تعين عدد للأسماء الحسنى تتعين به

TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r3.claim: The author enumerates the divine names found in the Qur'an, grouping them alphabetically by their Arabic initials.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r3.anchor: والذي ورد منها في لفظ الكتاب الإلهي مائة وبضعة 127 وعشرون اسما هي

TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r4.claim: The names belong to God essentially and originally; others possess their meanings only derivatively by God's gift, and that gift does not remove them from God's ownership.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#8/r4.anchor: فهو المالك لها حقيقة، وليس لغيره إلا ما ملكه الله من ذلك

TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r1.claim: Comparative forms such as al-Aʿlā and al-Akram, and genitive forms such as best of judges and providers, imply that divine and human referents share a basic meaning.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r1.anchor: فإن صيغة التفضيل تدل بظاهرها على اشتراك المفضل والمفضل عليه في أصل المعنى

TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r2.claim: There is no exegetical proof that divine names are restricted to transmitted forms; the opposing argument assumes both a covenantal reading of the article and that illicit naming means exceeding transmitted names, and both assumptions are questionable.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r2.anchor: وكلا الأمرين مورد نظر لما مر بيانه

TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r3.claim: The well-known report that God has ninety-nine names and that whoever enumerates them enters Paradise does not prove that names are restricted to that number.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r3.anchor: إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحدا من أحصاها دخل الجنة

TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r4.claim: Exegetically the names are not restricted to transmitted forms, while legal caution favors using only transmitted names for formal naming; ordinary predication is less restricted.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r4.anchor: والاحتياط في الدين يقتضي الاقتصار في التسمية بما ورد من طريق السمع

TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r5.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r5.claim: A report transmitted in al-Tawḥīd through al-Riḍā and his forefathers says that invoking God by ninety-nine names brings a response and enumerating them leads to Paradise; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī explains enumeration as faith in all their meanings.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r5.anchor: عن الرضا عن آبائه عن علي عليه السلام إن لله عز وجل تسعة وتسعين اسما

TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet's saying that God has ninety-nine names and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise, for God is singular and loves the singular.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#9/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r1.claim: Abū Nuʿaym and Ibn Mardawayh transmit from Abū Hurayra a variant saying that God has one hundred names less one, and that calling on them brings a response; al-Dāraquṭnī gives a divine-speech variant of the ninety-nine-name report.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r1.anchor: أقول رواها عن أبي نعيم وابن مردويه عنه، ولفظه قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn ʿUmar report the Prophet saying that God has ninety-nine names and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise; one wording adds that they are in the Qur'an.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r2.anchor: أخرج أبو نعيم وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس وابن عمر قالا قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r3.claim: The claim that all ninety-nine enumerated names occur in the Qur'an conflicts with later lists containing names not found there verbatim, unless it means that their meanings occur in the Qur'an.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r3.anchor: والرواية تعارض ما سيأتي من روايات الإحصاء حيث إن جميعها مشتملة على أسماء ليست في القرآن بلفظها

TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r4.claim: A report in al-Tawḥīd, transmitted through al-Ṣādiq's forebears from ʿAlī, repeats the Prophet's statement that God has ninety-nine names and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#10/r4.anchor: عن الصادق عن آبائه عن علي عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:7:180-186#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#11/r1.claim: The passage continues the transmitted enumeration of divine names, including Allah, al-Ilāh, al-Wāḥid, al-Aḥad, al-Ṣamad, and al-Awwal.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#11/r1.anchor: وهي الله، الإله، الواحد، الأحد، الصمد، الأول، الآخر، السميع، البصير، القدير

TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r1.claim: Allah is included in enumerations so that the other names can be predicated of Him; it is otherwise outside the count.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r1.anchor: وذكر لفظ الجلالة في هذه الروايات المشتملة على الإحصاء لإجراء الأسماء عليه

TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r2.claim: The quoted report repeats that God has ninety-nine names and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r2.anchor: إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما من أحصاها دخل الجنة

TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله جعفر بن محمد الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r3.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says the ninety-nine names are found in the Qur'an and assigns them to individual suras, listing five in al-Fātiḥa and thirty-three in al-Baqara among others.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#12/r3.anchor: عن الأسماء التسعة والتسعين التي من أحصاها دخل الجنة فقال هي في القرآن

TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r1.claim: The sura-by-sura report is confused: it counts Allah among the names, repeats names such as al-Kabīr, totals 110 despite initially saying ninety-nine, and disputes whether some names occur in the cited suras.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r1.anchor: فإن فيه إدخال لفظ الجلالة في الأسماء التسعة والتسعين وليس منها، وقد كرر بعض الأسماء

TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r2.claim: The available enumeration reports do not restrict God's beautiful names to their lists: they disagree, include names absent verbatim from the Qur'an, and omit Qur'anic names; at most, ninety-nine names carry the special promise of response and Paradise.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r2.anchor: لا تدل على انحصار الأسماء الحسنى فيما تحصيها مع ما فيها من الاختلاف في الأسماء

TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r3.claim: Other reports and transmitted prayers of the Prophet and the Imams show that God's names exceed ninety-nine and include many names absent from the Qur'anic enumeration lists.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r3.anchor: أن هناك روايات أخرى تدل على كون أسمائه تعالى أكثر من تسعة وتسعين

TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r4.claim: A report in al-Kāfī describes a nonphysical, unspoken divine name with four simultaneous parts: three names were revealed to meet creation's needs and one hidden, stored name was concealed; each revealed name has four pillars, each producing thirty names or acts.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#13/r4.anchor: إن الله تبارك وتعالى خلق اسما بالحروف غير متصوت، وباللفظ غير منطق

TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r1.claim: The report says the names ultimately reach 360, related to the three revealed names that serve as pillars and conceal the hidden name, and cites the command to call God by Allah or al-Raḥmān.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r1.anchor: فهذه الأسماء وما كان من الأسماء الحسنى حتى تتم ثلاثمائة وستين اسما

TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r2.claim: The described name cannot be a word or a mental concept; it is the referent matched by a word, namely the transcendent essence or something inseparable from it.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r2.anchor: فليس المراد بالاسم إلا المصداق المطابق للفظ لو كان هناك لفظ

TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r3.claim: Creating a name means the divine essence manifests in a way that yields a name, fitting the hierarchy in which names mediate for one another and end at a name whose determination is itself undetermined.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r3.anchor: أن المراد به ظهور الذات المتعالية ظهورا ينشأ به اسم من الأسماء

TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r4.claim: Allah, Tabāraka, and Taʿālā point respectively to the essence gathering all perfection, the affirmation of perfections and bestowal of blessings, and the removal of deficiencies and needs.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r4.anchor: وهي ثلاث جهة استجماع الذات لكل كمال

TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r5.claim: The report's names attributed as acts to the pillars express the author's principle that one name gives rise to another.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r5.anchor: وهو إشارة إلى ما قدمناه من انتشاء إسم من اسم

TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r6.claim: The report's count of 360 names explicitly shows that divine names are not limited to ninety-nine.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r6.anchor: صريح في عدم انحصار الأسماء الإلهية في تسعة وتسعين

TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r7.claim: The concealed name is still a manifestation of the divine essence, yet its hiddenness means its manifestation and determination are absent; even the claim that God exceeds every description remains a human description that cannot encompass Him.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#14/r7.anchor: فظهوره عين عدم ظهوره وتعينه عين عدم تعينه

TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r1.claim: The divine name Allah, which reveals the essence gathering every perfection, is one name of the Essence beneath the hidden stored name; Allah, al-Tabarak and al-Ta'ala veil that hidden name, while the Essence exceeds every name or sign.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r1.anchor: اسم الجلالة الكاشف عن الذات المستجمعة لجميع صفات الكمال اسما من أسماء الذات دونها ودون هذا الاسم المكنون المخزون

TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r2.claim: He infers this from 17:110: the conditional pronoun refers to an unspecified any, and the names denote their referents, so all names are related to an utterly unreportable and unindicated station.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r2.anchor: وجه الاستفادة أن الضمير في قوله { فله } راجع إلى " أي " وهو اسم شرط من الكنايات لا تعين لمعناه إلا عدم التعين

TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r3.claim: A transmitted account counts Tabarak, Ta'ala and the phrase that neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him among the divine names, using name in the broad sense of denoting an essence through an attribute.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r3.anchor: وهو مبني على مجرد الدلالة على الذات المأخوذة بصفة من صفاته من غير رعاية المصطلح الأدبي.

TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r4.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r4.claim: The Greatest Name has seventy-three letters; Asif possessed one, spoke it to bring Bilqis's throne across the collapsed earth, and the Imams possess seventy-two while God alone keeps one in the unseen.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r4.anchor: وفي البصائر بإسناده عن الباقر عليه السلام قال ان اسم الله الأعظم على ثلاثه وسبعين حرفا

TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r5.claim: A second report apportions the Greatest Name's seventy-three letters among Adam, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad, with Muhammad receiving seventy-two and God withholding one.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#15/r5.anchor: وفيه أيضا بإسناده عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن الله عز وجل جعل اسمه الأعظم على ثلاث وسبعون حرفا

TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r1.claim: The Greatest Name's seventy-three parts need not be literal alphabet letters: it is one name apportioned among prophets, whereas parts of an ordinary word would have no independent benefit.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r1.anchor: ولا ينبغي أن يرتاب في أن كونه مفرقا إلى ثلاثة وسبعين حرفا أو مؤلفا من حروف لا يستلزم كونه بحقيقة مؤلفا من حروف الهجاء

TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r2.claim: Ali's sermon affirms the core meanings of God's attributes while denying creaturely instances, material limits and deficiencies.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r2.anchor: أقول هو عليه السلام - كما يشاهد - يثبت في صفاته وأسمائه تعالى أصل المعاني وينفي خصوصيات المصاديق الممكنة ونواقص المادة

TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r3.claim: God has no likeness, equal or counterpart; the beautiful names belong uniquely to Him, and people who place them wrongly do so ignorantly, as in the verse about belief mixed with association.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r3.anchor: عن حنان بن سدير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في حديث فليس له شبه ولا مثل ولا عدل

TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r4.claim: He explains that no other being may be described by the perfected meanings reserved for God, such as applying Creator in its true sense to another.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r4.anchor: أي لا يوصف بالمعاني التي جردت لها وصح تسميته بها غيره تعالى كإطلاق الخالق

TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r5.claim: Abu Abd Allah says that the Imams are God's beautiful names, through knowledge of whom alone God accepts servants' deeds.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#16/r5.anchor: أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها } قال نحن والله الأسماء الحسنى

TABATABAI:7:180-186#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:180-186#17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:180-186#17/r1.claim: Name here means any indicator, verbal or otherwise; the prophets and successors are signs between God and creation and, through their complete servitude, manifestations of divine names and attributes.
TABATABAI:7:180-186#17/r1.anchor: أخذ الاسم بمعنى ما دل على الشيء سواء كان لفظا أو غيره، وعليه فالأنبياء والأوصياء عليهم السلام أسماء دالة عليه تعالى وسائط بينه وبين خلقه

ZAJJAJ:v2p392/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p392/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p392/r1.claim: Invoke God only by names He has used of Himself or by which He has described Himself; examples include Allah, al-Raḥmān, al-Jawād, al-Raḥīm, and al-Qawī, but not Subḥān, al-Rafīq, or al-Jild.
ZAJJAJ:v2p392/r1.anchor: لا ينبغي أن يدعوه أحد بما لم يصف نفسه به، أو لم يسم به نفسه

TABRISI:7:179-180/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:179-180/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:179-180/r8.claim: God's names are best because their meanings are good, such as the Generous, Merciful, Provider, and Noble; all of God's names are good and meaningful.
TABRISI:7:179-180/r8.anchor: أخبر سبحانه أن له الأسماء الحسنى لحسن معانيها مثل الجواد والرحيم والرازق والكريم

TABRISI:7:179-180/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:179-180/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:179-180/r9.claim: The names include essential attributes, active attributes, and names that declare God free of deficiency.
TABRISI:7:179-180/r9.anchor: فمنها ما يرجع إلى صفات ذاته كالعالم والقادر والحي والإله والقديم والسميع والبصير

TABRISI:7:179-180/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:179-180/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:7:179-180/r10.claim: Another interpretation says “the best names” are those whose mention comforts people, such as forgiveness and mercy rather than anger and punishment.
TABRISI:7:179-180/r10.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالحسنى ما مالت إليه النفوس من ذكر العفو والرحمة دون السخط والنقمة.

TABRISI:7:179-180/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:179-180/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:179-180/r11.claim: Calling upon God by the best names means invoking Him with names such as Allah, al-Rahman, al-Rahim, and Creator of the heavens and earth.
TABRISI:7:179-180/r11.anchor: أي بهذه الأسماء الحسنى ودعاؤه بها أن يقال يا الله يا رحمن يا رحيم

TABRISI:7:180-181/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:180-181/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:180-181/r1.claim: He cites a report in Muslim’s Ṣaḥīḥ that whoever enumerates God’s ninety-nine names enters Paradise; it describes God as One who loves oddness.
TABRISI:7:180-181/r1.anchor: إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة إلا واحدا من أحصاها دخل الجنة إنه وتر يحب الوتر

TABRISI:7:180-181/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:180-181/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
TABRISI:7:180-181/r2.claim: The idolaters deviated from God’s names by deriving al-Lāt from Allah, al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz, and Manāt from al-Mannān.
TABRISI:7:180-181/r2.anchor: فاشتقوا اللات من الله والعزى من العزيز ومنات من المنان عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

TABRISI:7:180-181/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:180-181/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:180-181/r3.claim: A broader interpretation is that they attribute to God descriptions or names that do not befit Him or may not be used for Him.
TABRISI:7:180-181/r3.anchor: إن معنى يلحدون في أسمائه يصفونه بما لا يليق به ويسمونه بما لا يجوز تسميته به

TABRISI:7:180-181/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:180-181/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:7:180-181/r4.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī includes calling Jesus God’s son among the forbidden ways of naming God; the author says this broader reading has wider benefit.
TABRISI:7:180-181/r4.anchor: وهذا الوجه أعم فائدة ويدخل فيه قول الجبائي أراد تسميتهم المسيح بأنه ابن الله

TABRISI:7:180-181/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:180-181/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:180-181/r5.claim: The verse indicates that God may be named only by the names He has applied to Himself.
TABRISI:7:180-181/r5.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أنه لا يجوز أن يسمى الله تعالى إلا بما سمى به نفسه

TABRISI:7:180-181/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:180-181/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:180-181/r6.claim: The threat of recompense applies in the Hereafter; another view extends it to this world and the Hereafter.
TABRISI:7:180-181/r6.anchor: في الآخرة. وقيل: في الدنيا والآخرة.

THALABI:v4p310/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r1.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v4p310/r1.claim: A man invoked God in prayer as both Allah and al-Rahman, prompting a Meccan polytheist to object that Muhammad's followers claimed one Lord but invoked two; the verse was revealed in response.
THALABI:v4p310/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: وذلك أن رجلا دعا الله في صلاته ودعا الرحمن، فقال رجل من مشركي مكة

THALABI:v4p310/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p310/r2.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine form corresponding to al-aḥsan, like al-kubrā and al-akbar; the beautiful names include al-Raḥmān, al-Raḥīm, al-Malik, al-Quddūs, and al-Salām.
THALABI:v4p310/r2.anchor: وهو تأنيث الأحسن كالكبرى والأكبر والصغرى والأصغر، والأسماء الحسنى هي الرحمن الرحيم

THALABI:v4p310/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v4p310/r3.claim: The Prophet said God has ninety-nine names, one short of a hundred, and whoever enumerates them all enters Paradise; no grading is stated.
THALABI:v4p310/r3.anchor: الأعرج عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن لله تبارك وتعالى تسعة وتسعين اسما، مائة غير واحدة، من أحصاها كلها دخل الجنة»

THALABI:v4p310/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p310/r4.claim: He glosses those who deviate in God's names as people who deny or lie.

THALABI:v4p310/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r5.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v4p310/r5.claim: He glosses deviation in God's names as associating partners with Him.

THALABI:v4p310/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r6.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v4p310/r6.claim: He gives the gloss ظامئون for those who deviate in God's names.

THALABI:v4p310/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r7.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v4p310/r7.claim: He says they turn away from the truth.
THALABI:v4p310/r7.anchor: زيد بن أسلم: يميلون عن الحق.

THALABI:v4p310/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
THALABI:v4p310/r8.claim: They identify those who deviate in God's names as the polytheists, who assigned divine names to idols and altered the names by adding or subtracting from them.
THALABI:v4p310/r8.anchor: ابن عباس ومجاهد: هم المشركون. وإلحادهم في أسماء الله عز وجل أنهم عدلوا بها عما هي عليه

THALABI:v4p310/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p310/r9.claim: The polytheists derived al-Lāt from Allah, al-ʿUzzā from al-ʿAzīz, and Manāt from al-Mannān.
THALABI:v4p310/r9.anchor: فاشتقوا اللات من الله تعالى والعزى من العزيز ومنات من المنان.

THALABI:v4p310/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r10.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v4p310/r10.claim: They define deviation in God's names as naming Him with a name He did not give Himself, which neither scripture names nor a messenger teaches.
THALABI:v4p310/r10.anchor: الإلحاد في أسماء الله تعالى يسميه بما لم يسم به ولا ينطق به كتاب ولا دعا إليه رسول

THALABI:v4p310/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p310/r11.claim: The root of ilḥād is to incline or depart from the right course; the same root describes a grave niche.
THALABI:v4p310/r11.anchor: وأصل الإلحاد الميل والعدول عن القصد ومنه لحد القبر.

THALABI:v4p310/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r12.speaker: يحيى بن رئاب والأعمش وحمزة
THALABI:v4p310/r12.claim: They read the verb with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ here and in al-Naḥl.
THALABI:v4p310/r12.anchor: فقرأ يحيى بن رئاب والأعمش وحمزة: بفتح الياء والحاء هاهنا وفي النحل

THALABI:v4p310/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p310/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p310/r13.claim: The remaining readers pronounce the verb with ḍamma on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ; both forms are valid Arabic.
THALABI:v4p310/r13.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بضم الياء وكسر الحاء وهما لغتان [صحيحتان]

THALABI:v4p311/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p311/r1.speaker: الكسائي
THALABI:v4p311/r1.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the verb in al-Naḥl with fatḥa on yāʾ and ḥāʾ, but reads its form in al-Aʿrāf with ḍamma.
THALABI:v4p311/r1.anchor: وأما الكسائي فإنه قرأ التي في النحل بفتح الياء والحاء وفي الأعراف (رحم) بالضم

THALABI:v4p311/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p311/r2.speaker: الكسائي
THALABI:v4p311/r2.claim: He distinguishes ilḥād as deviation from the right course and laḥd or luḥūd as leaning; he understands the al-Naḥl form as leaning.
THALABI:v4p311/r2.anchor: فيقول: الإلحاد العديل عن القصد واللحد واللحود الركون، ويزعم أن التي في النحل يعني الركون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
