WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r1.claim: The commentators cite Abū Hurayra's report from the Prophet that God has ninety-nine names, one short of a hundred; the revealed names are bounded and known through religious authority, as indicated by the definite wording.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: (هي ما ذكره أبو هريرة عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال: "إن لله تبارك وتعالى تسعة وتسعين اسما مائة غير واحدة"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r2.claim: Calling upon God by these names means honoring Him through invocation such as O Powerful, O Knowing, and O Generous.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فادعوه بها}؛ دعاؤه بها تعظيمه بذكرها؛ كقولك: يا قدير يا عليم يا كريم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq says one should not call God by a name or attribute He did not use of Himself, such as generous, gentle, or strong-bodied, even when the proposed word is offered as a synonym.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬1): إلا ينبغي أنا تدعوه بما لم يصف به نفسه أو لم يسم به نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r4.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r4.claim: Another authority says one of the best forms of supplication is to invoke God by His beautiful names, as He commands here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p478#2/r4.anchor: وقال غيره: (في هذه الآية دليل على أن من أفضل الدعاء أن تدعوا الله بالأسماء الحسنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r1.speaker: حمزة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads yalḥidūn; ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī agree with this form in al-Naḥl, and al-Farrāʾ treats yalḥidūn and yalḥadūn as two language forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r1.anchor: وقرأ (¬3) حمزة: {يلحدون}، ووافقه عاصم (¬4) والكسائي في النحل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r2.claim: The lexicographers define ilḥād as turning away from the proper course.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r2.anchor: قال أهل اللغة (¬1): (معنى الإلحاد في اللغة: الميل عن القصد)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt defines a heretic as one who deviates from truth and inserts into religion what does not belong there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r3.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت: (الملحد العادل عن الحق المدخل فيه ما ليس فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r4.speaker: غيره من أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r4.claim: Other lexicographers define it as deviation from uprightness and connect it with the side niche of a grave, unlike a central trench.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r4.anchor: وقال غيره من أهل اللغة: (الإلحاد العدل عن الاستقامة والانحراف عنها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r5.claim: Al-Wāḥidī prefers the common reading, supported by the Qur'anic use of ilḥād in the sanctuary; ilḥād is more common in Arabic, and reading both forms can encompass both language variants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r5.anchor: والأجود قراءة العامة؛ لقوله تعالى: {ومن يرد فيه بإلحاد} [الحج: 25]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identify the people who deviate in God's names as polytheists who applied divine names to idols, altering them or deriving al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt from God's names.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد (¬2): ({الذين يلحدون في أسمائه} هم المشركون، عدلوا بأسماء الله عما هي عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r7.claim: The scholars of meaning define them as those who call God by names He did not give Himself in scripture or through a Messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r7.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (الذين يلحدون في أسماء الله الذين (¬3) يسمون الله بما لم يسم به نفسه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses deviation in God's names as lying.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r8.anchor: ما روى عن ابن عباس أنه قال: ({يلحدون في أسمائه} أي: يكذبون)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r9.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says they turn away from the truth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r9.anchor: وقال زيد بن أسلم: (يميلون عن الحق)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r10.claim: Al-Wāḥidī concludes that anyone assigning God a name without revealed authorization lies in that naming and departs from truth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p480/r10.anchor: فكل من سمى الله بما لم يرد به توقيف فقد كذب في ذلك (¬2) التسمية ومال عن الحق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p483/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p483/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p483/r1.claim: Those who deviate in God's names will receive in the Hereafter recompense for the deeds they used to do.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p483/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {سيجزون ما كانوا يعملون} أي: جزاء ما كانوا يعملون في الآخرة

ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n145/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n145/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n145/r1.claim: The verse follows the heedless ones of 7:179: they fail to discern as intended and ignore God, who embodies all perfection and is Ultimate Reality.
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n145/r1.anchor: This passage connects with the mention, at the end of the preceding verse, of "the heedless ones" who do not use their faculty of discernment

ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n145/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n145/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n145/r2.claim: Asma al-husna means God's attributes of perfection: ism denotes substance or intrinsic attributes, al-husna is the plural of al-ahsan, and the term is reserved for God.
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n145/r2.anchor: the term ism is, primarily, a word applied to denote the substance or the intrinsic attributes of an object under consideration

ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n146/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n146/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n146/r1.claim: Razi explains distortion of God's names as applying them to other beings or defining God through anthropomorphic relations such as father or son.
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n146/r1.anchor: by applying them to other beings or objects or, alternatively, by trying to "define" God in anthropomorphic terms and relationships, like "father" or "son" (Razi)

ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n147/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n147/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n147/r1.claim: The promise of requital includes the righteous of every era and community who receive God's messages and live by conviction that He is Ultimate Reality; this broadens the earlier example of Moses' people.
ASAD-NOTES:7:180#n147/r1.anchor: the reference is broadened to include the righteous of all times and communities - that is, all those who are receptive to God's messages

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r8.claim: God's beautiful names are the ninety-nine names.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r8.anchor: ولله الأسماء الحسنى } يعني: التسعة والتسعين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r9.claim: People should call upon God with these names, such as Allah, the Powerful, and the Knowing.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r9.anchor: فادعوه بها } كقولك: يا الله، يا قدير، يا عليم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r10.claim: Those who deviate in God's names are polytheists who repurposed names for idols, adding or subtracting and deriving al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat from divine names.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r10.anchor: وهم المشركون عدلوا بأسماء الله عما هي عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r11.claim: They will receive recompense for their deeds in the afterlife.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:179-180/r11.anchor: جزاء ما كانوا يعملون في الآخرة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r1.claim: Bint al-Shati says later interpreters generally stay within earlier explanations of the disjoint letters, selecting one and elaborating it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r1.anchor: ولا يكاد المتأخرون يخرجون عن تلك الأقوال، إلا أن يختاروا قولاً منها يزيدونه تفصيلاً وبياناً وإيضاحاً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr is reported to say the letters are God's names separated into parts; knowing their arrangement would reveal the greatest name, though Ibn Abbas says their arrangement is unknown.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r2.anchor: ورووا عن سعيد بن جبير أنها أسماء الله تعالى مقطعة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r3.claim: Other interpretations take the letters as the name of an angel or a prophet, or as signs and keys to God's beautiful names, with individual letters standing for divine names.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r3.anchor: أو هي اسم ملك من ملائكته تعالى، أو نبي من أنبيائه. وعند بعضهم أن حروف الفواتح دوالّ على أسماء الله الحسنى أو مفاتيح لها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says most interpreters regard the opening letters as names for the suras, meaning titles based on their opening words rather than literal names.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r4.anchor: وقيل، هي أسماء للسور التي افتتحت بها. قال "الزمخشري" في الكشاف: "وعليه - أي على هذا الوجه - إطباق الأكثر"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r5.claim: Related explanations call the letters names of the Quran, like al-Furqan, or symbols for its names; one account says revelation scribes placed them as signs.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p143/r5.anchor: وقريب من هذا، قول من قال إن الفواتح من أسماء القرآن، كالفرقان. ومن تأويلها رموزاً لأسمائه، القول بأنها علامات وضعها كُتَّاب الوحي

NASHR:v1p486/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p486/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p486/r1.claim: Naql is Abū al-Fatḥ al-Mahdawī’s and Ibn Shurayḥ’s position, followed by most performance authorities and listed as the second option in al-Taysīr and al-Shāṭibiyya.
NASHR:v1p486/r1.anchor: (والثاني) النقل وهو مذهب أبي الفتح فارس بن أحمد المهدوي، وابن شريح أيضا، والجمهور

NASHR:v1p486/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p486/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p486/r2.claim: The proposed third option, full realization without sakt, lacks a known textual or transmitted route from Ḥamza; predecessors agree on naql at pause, and using it for Khallād based on later commentary is unsupported.
NASHR:v1p486/r2.anchor: وحكي فيه وجه ثالث، وهو التحقيق من غير سكت كالجماعة، ولا أعلمه نصا في كتاب من الكتب ولا في طريق من الطرق

NASHR:v1p486/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p486/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p486/r3.claim: For «ولله الأسماء الحسنى» and similar forms, ten transmitted options combine naql or sakt with five methods for the final hamza; no-sakt/no-naql is excluded as unsupported.
NASHR:v1p486/r3.anchor: مسألة (ولله الأسماء الحسنى) ونحوه يصح فيه عشرة أوجه، وهي الوجهان المذكوران

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p20#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p20#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p20#2/r1.claim: Ilḥād in God's names means deviating from the truth, including invoking al-Lāt, al-ʿUzzā, and similar idols.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p20#2/r1.anchor: والإلحاد (2) في أسمائه: [الجور عن الحق والعدول عنه، وذكر] اللات والعزى، وأشباه ذلك.

BURHAN:v1p10/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p10/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p10/r1.claim: In the introduction, Zarkashī's outline ranges from surah endings and revelation history through readings, pauses, virtues, abrogation, ambiguity, inimitability, and exegesis among the Qur'anic sciences.
BURHAN:v1p10/r1.anchor: الثامن : في خواتم السور . التاسع : في معروفة المكي والمدني . العاشر : معرفة أول ما نزل

BURHAN:v1p172/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p172/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p172/r1.claim: The disjointed initials are written as letter forms rather than letter names to follow the established spelling convention, paralleling ordinary writing.
BURHAN:v1p172/r1.anchor: علل ذلك بأن الكلمة لما كانت مركبة من ذوات الحروف واستمرت العادة متى تهجيت ومتى قيل للكاتب اكتب كيت وكيت أن يلفظ بالأسماء وتقع فى الكتابة الحروف أنفسها

BURHAN:v1p172/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p172/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p172/r2.claim: Their public familiarity, unspelled recitation, and single-letter forms prevent confusion; unusual codex spellings do not harm recitation or memorization, and the codex script is followed as Sunnah.
BURHAN:v1p172/r2.anchor: وأيضا فإن شهرة أمرها وإقامة ألسنة الأحمر والأسود لها وأن اللافظ بها غير متهجاة لا يجىء بطائل فيها وأن بعضها مفرد لا يخطر ببال غير ما هو عليه

BURHAN:v1p172/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p172/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p172/r3.claim: The first position treats the initials as a hidden secret reserved to God; Abū Bakr says every book has a secret and the Qur'an's secret is its opening letters.
BURHAN:v1p172/r3.anchor: ولهذا قال الصديق رضى الله عنه فى كل كتاب سر وسره فى القرآن أوائل السور

BURHAN:v1p172/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p172/r4.speaker: الشعبي
BURHAN:v1p172/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbī classifies the initials among the ambiguous passages: affirm their apparent form and consign their knowledge to God.
BURHAN:v1p172/r4.anchor: قال الشعبى إنها من المتشابه نؤمن بظاهرها ونكل العلم فيها إلى الله عز وجل

BURHAN:v1p172/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p172/r5.speaker: الرازي
BURHAN:v1p172/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī reports theologians' objection that unintelligible Qur'anic words conflict with the command to reflect and infer meaning, while asking why speech could not test submission as unintelligible ritual acts do.
BURHAN:v1p172/r5.anchor: قال الإمام الرازى وقد أنكر المتكلمون هذا القول وقالوا لا يجوز أن يرد فى كتاب الله ما لا يفهمه الخلق لأن الله تعالى أمر بتدبره

BURHAN:v1p172/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p172/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p172/r6.claim: The second position holds that the initials have known meanings; more than twenty explanations are offered, ranging from remote to plausible.
BURHAN:v1p172/r6.anchor: القول الثانى أن المراد منها معلوم وذكروا فيه ما يزيد على عشرين وجها فمنها البعيد ومنها القريب

BURHAN:v1p172/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p172/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v1p172/r7.claim: A view transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās derives each initial from a divine name: for example, alif from Allah, lām from Laṭīf, and mīm from Majīd, or from His favors, gentleness, and glory.
BURHAN:v1p172/r7.anchor: ويروى عن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما أن كل حرف منها مأخوذ من اسم من أسمائه سبحانه فالألف من الله واللام من لطيف والميم من مجيد

BURHAN:v1p172/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p172/r8.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v1p172/r8.claim: Ibn Fāris calls the derivation of initials from divine names a good explanation and says Arabic usage provides supporting evidence.
BURHAN:v1p172/r8.anchor: قال ابن فارس وهذا وجه جيد وله فى كلام العرب شاهد

BURHAN:v1p173/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p173/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p173/r1.claim: The opening letters attest that Muhammad's recited Book is revealed and without doubt; as the basic material of expression shared across revealed languages, the letters merit an oath like the dawn and the mount.
BURHAN:v1p173/r1.anchor: أن هذا الكتاب الذى يقرؤه محمد هو الكتاب المنزل لا شك فيه وذلك يدل على جلالة قدر هذه الحروف

BURHAN:v1p173/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p173/r2.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
BURHAN:v1p173/r2.claim: The selected letters are keys to divine names, favors, trials, and peoples' lifespans; alif, lam, and mim signify one, thirty, and forty years. Ibn Faris calls this a fine, subtle view.
BURHAN:v1p173/r2.anchor: روى عن الربيع بن أنس قال ابن فارس وهو قول حسن لطيف لأن الله تعالى أنزل

BURHAN:v1p173/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p173/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v1p173/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ALM as I am God, the All-Knowing; ALMS as I am God, the Most Excellent; and ALR as I am God, the Seeing, illustrating a single letter's indication of a comprehensive name and perfect attribute.
BURHAN:v1p173/r3.anchor: يروى عن ابن عباس أيضا فى قوله تعالى ﴿ الم ﴾ أنا الله أعلم وفى ﴿ المص ﴾ أنا الله أفضل

BURHAN:v1p173/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p173/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p173/r4.claim: Many, including al-Zamakhshari, Sibawayh, and Fakhr al-Din, treat the opening letters as surah names that distinguish chapters; repeated ALM openings are differentiated by what follows, as in these two examples.
BURHAN:v1p173/r4.anchor: ونقله الزمخشرى عن الأكثرين وأن سيبويه نص عليه فى كتابه وقال الإمام فخر الدين هو قول أكثر المتكلمين

BURHAN:v1p173/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p173/r5.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v1p173/r5.claim: Ibn Faris says the surah openings are the Qur'an's secret; he understands this as a secret known only to God and those firmly grounded in knowledge, a view also chosen by a group including Ibn Hibban.
BURHAN:v1p173/r5.anchor: قال ابن فارس وأظن قائل ذلك أراد أنه من السر الذى لا يعلمه إلا الله والراسخون فى العلم

BURHAN:v1p395/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p395/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p395/r6.claim: The alif added to lengthen a vocative such as ya qawmi or ya ʿibadi is omitted because it only connects two levels, a subtle feature with no perceptible existence.
BURHAN:v1p395/r6.anchor: حذفت الألف الآتية لمد الصوت بالنداء مثل ﴿ يقوم ﴾ ﴿ يا عباد ﴾ لأنها زائدة للتوصل بين المرتبتين

ITQAN:v1p25/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p25/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p25/r1.claim: Because Qurʾanic sciences and meanings cannot be exhausted, the author compiles what is possible, aiming to open their fields and aid exegetes in reaching truths and some subtleties.
ITQAN:v1p25/r1.anchor: لما كانت علوم القرآن لا تحصى ومعانيه لا تستقصى وجبت العناية بالقدر الممكن

ITQAN:v1p25/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p25/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p25/r2.claim: The first listed fields cover occasions of revelation, links between verses, endings, homonyms and recurring senses, ambiguous passages, unidentified referents, opening and closing features, and Meccan-Medinan classification.
ITQAN:v1p25/r2.anchor: النوع الأول معرفة سبب النزول الثاني معرفة المناسبة بين الآيات الثالث معرفة الفواصل الرابع معرفة الوجوه والنظائر

ITQAN:v1p25/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p25/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p25/r3.claim: Further fields concern first revelation, languages, mode of descent, collection and preservation, division and names of the Qurʾān, non-Hijazi or non-Arabic vocabulary, and rare words.
ITQAN:v1p25/r3.anchor: العاشر في معرفة أول ما نزل

ITQAN:v1p25/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p25/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p25/r4.claim: The list includes morphology, legal rulings, eloquence, textual variants and their interpretation, pauses, orthography, virtues, special properties, and whether some passages excel others.
ITQAN:v1p25/r4.anchor: الحادي والعشرون معرفة كون اللفظ أو التركيب أحسن وأفصح

ITQAN:v1p25/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p25/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p25/r5.claim: The remaining listed subjects are recitation etiquette, Qurʾanic quotations in compositions, embedded proverbs, rulings, and Qurʾanic argumentation.
ITQAN:v1p25/r5.anchor: التاسع والعشرون في آداب تلاوته الثلاثون في أنه هل يجوز في التصانيف والرسائل والخطب استعمال بعض آيات القرآن

ITQAN:v1p27/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p27/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p27/r1.claim: The opening categories classify revelation by place, circumstances, time, season, sleep or bed, earth or heaven, first and last revelation, occasions, Companion speech, repetition, and delayed ruling or descent.
ITQAN:v1p27/r1.anchor: النوع الأول معرفة المكي والمدني الثاني معرفة الحضري والسفري الثالث النهاري والليلي الرابع الصيفي والشتائي

ITQAN:v1p27/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p27/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p27/r2.claim: Other descent categories distinguish piecemeal from collective revelation, accompanied from solitary revelation, revelation shared with earlier prophets, and the manner of descent.
ITQAN:v1p27/r2.anchor: الثالث عشر معرفة ما نزل مفرقا وما نزل جمعا الرابع عشر ما نزل مشيعا وما نزل مفردا

ITQAN:v1p27/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p27/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p27/r3.claim: The list covers Qurʾanic names and sūra names, collection and arrangement, counts of sūras, verses, words and letters, transmitters and memorizers, and high or low chains.
ITQAN:v1p27/r3.anchor: السابع عشر في معرفة أسمائه وأسماء سوره الثامن عشر في جمعه وترتيبه التاسع عشر في عدد سوره وآياته وكلماته وحروفه

ITQAN:v1p27/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p27/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p27/r4.claim: Transmission categories include mutawātir, famous, solitary, anomalous, fabricated, and interpolated material.
ITQAN:v1p27/r4.anchor: الثاني والعشرون معرفة المتواتر الثالث والعشرون في المشهور الرابع والعشرون في الآحاد الخامس والعشرون في الشاذ

ITQAN:v1p27/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p27/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p27/r5.claim: Performance and script fields include pauses and beginnings, connected wording with separate meaning, imāla, assimilation and related sound rules, lengthening, hamza easing, and learning practice.
ITQAN:v1p27/r5.anchor: الثامن والعشرون في معرفة الوقف والابتداء التاسع والعشرون في بيان الموصول لفظا المفصول معنى

ITQAN:v1p27/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p27/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p27/r6.claim: Further areas cover recitation etiquette, rare words, non-Hijazi and non-Arabic vocabulary, recurring senses, and particles needed by exegetes.
ITQAN:v1p27/r6.anchor: الرابع والثلاثون في كيفية تحمله الخامس والثلاثون في آداب تلاوته السادس والثلاثون في معرفة غريبه

ITQAN:v1p27/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p27/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p27/r7.claim: The final entries treat parsing, essential exegetical principles, clear and ambiguous passages, and precedence or postponement.
ITQAN:v1p27/r7.anchor: الأربعون في معرفة معاني الأدوات التي يحتاج إليها المفسر الحادي والأربعون في معرفة إعرابه

ITQAN:v2p445#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r1.claim: The common analysis of Allāhumma is “O God”: the vocative yā is omitted and replaced by the doubled mīm at the end.
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r1.anchor: المشهور أن معناه يا الله حذفت ياء النداء وعوض عنها الميم المشددة في آخره

ITQAN:v2p445#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r2.claim: Another etymology derives it from “yā Allāh, secure us with good,” compounded like ḥayyahalā.
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r2.anchor: وقيل أصله يا الله أمنا بخير فركب تركيب حيهلا

ITQAN:v2p445#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r3.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r3.claim: Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī says the mīm gathers seventy of God’s names.
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو رجاء العطادي الميم فيها تجمع سبعين اسما من أسمائه

ITQAN:v2p445#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r4.speaker: ابن ظفر
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ẓafar reports the view that Allāhumma is the Greatest Name: Allāh denotes the divine essence and the mīm denotes the ninety-nine attributes.
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن ظفر قيل إنها الاسم الأعظم واستدل لذلك بأن الله دال على الذات والميم دالة على الصفات التسعة والتسعين

ITQAN:v2p445#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī says Allāhumma encompasses supplication.
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r5.anchor: ولهذا قال الحسن البصري اللهم تجمع الدعاء

ITQAN:v2p445#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r6.speaker: النضر بن شميل
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r6.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl says that whoever says Allāhumma has invoked God by all His names.
ITQAN:v2p445#2/r6.anchor: وقال النضر بن شميل من قال اللهم فقد دعا الله بجميع أسمائه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p257/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p257/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p257/r1.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the feminine form faʿlā from ḥusn, used for a single blessing or act of kindness.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p257/r1.anchor: الحسنى : فعلى من الحسن ، يقال : في النعمة الواحدة ، أو الفعلة الواحدة من الإحسان .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p257/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p257/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p257/r6.claim: In the verse about God’s names, al-ḥusnā means the highest or most exalted.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p257/r6.anchor: والخامس : العليا ، ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

BURHAN:v2p451/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p451/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p451/r1.claim: Feminine singular adjectives can describe feminine plural nouns; examples include السماوات العلى, الأسماء الحسنى, and القرون الأولى.
BURHAN:v2p451/r1.anchor: وإنما وصف الجمع بالمفرد لآن اللفظ المؤنث يجوز إطلاقه على جماعة المؤنث بخلاف لفظ المذكر

NASHR:v2p273/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p273/r8.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v2p273/r8.claim: Hamza reads يلحدون with fatḥa on yāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ at all three locations.
NASHR:v2p273/r8.anchor: فقرأ حمزة بفتح الياء وكسر الحاء في ثلاثهن

BIQAI-FULL:v3p180/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p180/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p180/r2.claim: The command to call upon God by His beautiful names echoes the earlier command to call upon Him humbly and privately.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p180/r2.anchor: ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها } ) 77 [ الأعراف : 180 ] هو - { ادعوا ربكم تضرعا وخفية }
